current_declaration.title: Finite-Jet Non-Abelian BRST Complex
current_declaration.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty open set with coordinates $x^1,\ldots,x^n$, and let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra with bilinear alternating bracket $[\ ,\ ]_{\mathfrak g}$ satisfying the Jacobi identity. Let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex vector space, and let $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ be an even representation, meaning $\rho([X,Y]_{\mathfrak g})=\rho(X)\rho(Y)-\rho(Y)\rho(X)$ for all $X,Y\in\mathfrak g$ and each $\rho(X)$ preserves the grading of $V$. This is local Lie-algebra data; no global group, principal bundle, action functional, or quantum theory is selected here.

Choose a basis $T_a$ of $\mathfrak g$ and write $[T_b,T_c]_{\mathfrak g}=f^a{}_{bc}T_a$. A local gauge potential is a $\mathfrak g$-valued one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$ whose component jet generators $A_{\mu,I}^a$ are even and have ghost number zero. A matter field is a $V$-valued local field $\psi$ with each component jet generator $\psi_I^\alpha$ assigned the parity of its graded component and ghost number zero. The ghost is $c=c^aT_a$, with odd component jet generators $c_I^a$ of ghost number one. The coefficient bracket of homogeneous $\mathfrak g$-valued fields is $[X,Y]^a=f^a{}_{bc}X^bY^c$, using multiplication in the graded-commutative coefficient algebra; in particular $[c,c]^a=f^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$ has no factor of $1/2$.

For a multi-index $I=(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\in\mathbb N^n$, let $\Phi_I$ denote the corresponding formal jet generator of a field component $\Phi$. The finite-jet local algebra $\mathcal F_U$ is $C^\infty(U)$ tensored with the polynomial algebra in its even jet generators and the exterior algebra in its odd jet generators, where each element uses only finitely many jet generators. The total derivatives $D_\mu$ act by $D_\mu f=\partial_\mu f$ on $f\in C^\infty(U)$ and $D_\mu\Phi_I=\Phi_{I+e_\mu}$ on every jet generator; the multi-index derivatives commute.

Define the degree-one BRST operator candidate $s$ on the fields by

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\frac12[c,c],\qquad s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi.$$

On coefficient functions set $sf=0$, and on every jet generator set $s(\Phi_I)=D_I(s\Phi)$; extend $s$ to $\mathcal F_U$ by the odd left-derivation rule $s(FG)=(sF)G+(-1)^{|F|}F(sG)$ for homogeneous $F$, where $|F|$ is total parity. The minimal sector here contains only $A,\psi,c$ and their jets. Antighosts and Nakanishi–Lautrup variables are not included; adjoining such a nonminimal pair requires separate definitions and a proof before any cohomological triviality claim. The specified data are a BRST complex once $s^2=0$, which is established for these formulas in the following nilpotence lemma.

current_declaration.title: Adopted ABJM localization model on the round three-sphere
current_declaration.design_state: A-page adopted source-specific ABJM N=2 model on round S3, with exact global form, levels, field content, R-charges, zero deformations, contour, gauge fixing, and formal measure limit.
current_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix $r>0$ with units of length and the round oriented sphere
$$
\mathbb S^3_r=\{y\in\mathbb R^4:\textstyle\sum_{\alpha=1}^4 y_\alpha^2=r^2\}
$$
with its induced Riemannian metric, no boundary, and its unique spin structure. Adopt the source-specific ABJM model on this background, viewed through one chosen three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. Its gauge group is $G=U(N)\times U(N)$ with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and supersymmetric Chern–Simons levels $k$ and $-k$, where $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$. The global group includes both central $U(1)$ factors. Write $\operatorname{tr}_N$ for the trace in the defining representation of either factor; in the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov convention the level multiplies $\operatorname{tr}_N/(4\pi)$ in the supersymmetric Chern–Simons action.

Each $\mathcal N=2$ vector multiplet has a Hermitian matrix-valued connection $A_\mu$ (or $\widehat A_\mu$), a real Hermitian adjoint scalar $\sigma$ (or $\widehat\sigma$), a two-component complex gaugino $\lambda$ (or $\widehat\lambda$), and a real auxiliary scalar $D$ (or $\widehat D$). In an oriented coordinate chart the first factor's source-normalized action is
$$
S_{\mathrm{CS},k}=\frac{k}{4\pi}\int d^3x\,\operatorname{tr}_N\!\left(\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}\left(A_\mu\partial_\nu A_\rho+\frac{2i}{3}A_\mu A_\nu A_\rho\right)-\lambda^\dagger\lambda+2D\sigma\right);
$$
the second factor uses the same expression with $(A,\lambda,D,\sigma,k)$ replaced by $(\widehat A,\widehat\lambda,\widehat D,\widehat\sigma,-k)$. Here $\epsilon^{\mu\nu\rho}$ is the oriented Levi-Civita density.

The matter consists of two chiral multiplets $A_a$, $a=1,2$, in $(\mathbf N,\overline{\mathbf N})$ and two $B_{\dot a}$, $\dot a=1,2$, in $(\overline{\mathbf N},\mathbf N)$. A chiral multiplet means a complex scalar, a two-component complex spinor, and a complex auxiliary scalar in its stated representation. For $A_a$, for example, a gauge transformation $(U,\widehat U)\in G$ acts by $A_a\mapsto U A_a\widehat U^{-1}$; the $B_{\dot a}$ action is the reversed one. The covariant derivative on a bifundamental scalar is $D_\mu A_a=\partial_\mu A_a+iA_\mu A_a-iA_a\widehat A_\mu$; spinors also carry the Levi-Civita spin connection. The vector-multiplet fields act in that representation by left multiplication from the first factor minus right multiplication from the second.

The round-sphere component action for one chiral multiplet $(\phi,\psi,F)$ of $R$-charge $\Delta=\tfrac12$, in the representation determined by its bifundamental type, is
$$
S_{\mathrm{chiral}}=\int_{\mathbb S^3_r}d^3x\,\sqrt g\left((D_\mu\phi)^\dagger D^\mu\phi+\frac{3}{4r^2}\phi^\dagger\phi+i\psi^\dagger\gamma^\mu D_\mu\psi+F^\dagger F-\phi^\dagger\sigma^2\phi+\phi^\dagger D\phi-\psi^\dagger\sigma\psi+i\phi^\dagger\lambda^\dagger\psi-i\psi^\dagger\lambda\phi\right).
$$
The representation-valued $\sigma,D,\lambda$ in this expression act by the first-factor action minus the second-factor action. Sum this action over the four chiral multiplets.

The adopted $\mathcal N=2$ superpotential is
$$
W=\frac{2\pi}{k}\epsilon^{ab}\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_aB_{\dot a}A_bB_{\dot b})=\frac{4\pi}{k}\operatorname{tr}_N(A_1B_1A_2B_2-A_1B_2A_2B_1),
$$
where $\epsilon^{12}=1=-\epsilon^{21}$ and all other components vanish. The superpotential is the holomorphic interaction that supplies the chiral auxiliary-field and Yukawa terms. This is the ABJM quartic interaction; the adopted quantum model has the enhanced $\mathcal N=6$ superconformal symmetry, while localization uses only the selected $\mathcal N=2$ subalgebra. The scalar component of each chiral multiplet has $U(1)_R$ charge and superconformal dimension $\Delta=\tfrac12$; its fermion and auxiliary component have charges $\Delta-1$ and $\Delta-2$. Set all real masses and Fayet–Iliopoulos parameters to zero. A real mass here is the constant scalar in a background flavor vector multiplet; a Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter is the coefficient of the auxiliary $D$ field for an abelian vector multiplet. The level $k$ is dimensionless, $r$ has units of length, $[A_\mu]=[\sigma]=[\lambda]=r^{-1}$, $[D]=r^{-2}$, $[\phi]=r^{-1/2}$, $[\psi]=r^{-1}$, and $[F]=r^{-3/2}$.

The smooth field domain consists of pairs of smooth connections and the listed smooth associated matter and auxiliary fields on the trivial $U(N)\times U(N)$ bundles. The smooth gauge group $C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$ acts by the transformations just specified. The source gauge-fixes this quotient by the covariant Lorenz conditions $\nabla^\mu A_\mu=\nabla^\mu\widehat A_\mu=0$. Its Faddeev–Popov ghosts are anticommuting scalar fields representing the determinant of the derivative of these gauge conditions along gauge orbits. The Euclidean contour takes the vector connections and real scalars on their Hermitian/real slices, pairs each matter scalar with its Hermitian conjugate, and integrates the fermions as independent Grassmann variables. The diagonal Hermitian matrices form the Cartan subalgebras; the residual Weyl group $S_N\times S_N$, with $S_N$ the permutation group on $N$ entries, permutes their eigenvalues. The Cartan eigenvalues lie on real lines.

Choose a normalized conformal Killing spinor $\epsilon$ satisfying $\nabla_\mu\epsilon=\frac{i}{2r}\gamma_\mu\epsilon$ in an orthonormal frame, where $\gamma_\mu$ are Hermitian two-dimensional gamma matrices. Let $Q$ be its off-shell supersymmetry transformation and let $\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ be the Faddeev–Popov differential. In the source gauge-fixed complex, $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}=Q+\delta_{\mathrm{FP}}$ is odd and squares to zero on the gauge-fixed fields and ghosts. The source localization calculation adds a dimensionless parameter $t$ times a $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-exact Yang–Mills deformation. Its one-loop determinants are zeta-regularized, with $\log\det L=-\zeta_L'(0)$ when the source's spectral hypotheses apply; they are the Gaussian boson/fermion/ghost determinant ratios about the constant-Cartan locus.

The corresponding gauge-fixed functional integral is only the formal expression
$$
Z_{\mathrm{formal}}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{vol}(\mathcal G)}\int_{\mathcal C/\mathcal G}[D\Phi]\,e^{-S_E[\Phi]},
$$
where $\mathcal G=C^\infty(\mathbb S^3_r,U(N)\times U(N))$, $\mathcal C$ is the source Euclidean contour, and $S_E$ is the supersymmetric Chern–Simons, chiral-matter, and superpotential action specified above. The source calculation assumes that its gauge-fixed measure and contour are $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$-invariant and that the deformation introduces no anomalous Jacobian (a multiplicative change of the formal measure under $Q_{\mathrm{gf}}$) or surface contribution at the boundary of field space. These are adopted formal field-theory inputs: this postulate does not construct an infinite-dimensional measure, prove convergence of the localization limit, or assert a theorem for arbitrary three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ models.

current_declaration.title: ADHM linear data, stability, costability and FI levels
current_declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\ge1$ and $k\ge0$ and standard Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$. A framed ADHM linear datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$ and $J:V\to W$. Define the complex and real polynomial expressions

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable if the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, with $m\ge0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$ and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable if there is no nonzero subspace of $V$ invariant under both $B_i$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular if it is stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. Its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$.

Write $X^s=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable}\}$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}=\{x\in X^s:x\text{ costable}\}$ and, for real $\zeta\ge0$, $X_\zeta^U=\{x\in X^s:\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=\zeta I_V\}$. Denote the corresponding orbit sets by $X^s/GL(V)$, $X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V)$ and $X_\zeta^U/U(V)$, with quotient topologies when discussing their analytic spaces. A word frame consists of $k$ columns obtained by fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard basis vectors of $W$.

For $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^2\times(\mathbb C^*)^N$, write $t_1,t_2,e_1,\ldots,e_N$ for the coordinate characters and put $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot x=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$. The compact torus is its subgroup on which all characters have modulus one. The framing representation thus has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$.

These are finite-dimensional matrix definitions. They do not assert a real/complex quotient correspondence, a sheaf or ASD identification, or a noncompact pushforward. In particular, positive-FI stability and zero-FI regularity are distinct conditions; neither an endpoint identification nor an ordinary ASD interpretation follows from this definition.

current_declaration.title: Donaldson's ADHM matrix equations in the source convention
current_declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. Write $\alpha_1,\alpha_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $P:W\to V$, and $Q:V\to W$. The Donaldson source convention for these four matrices is

$$[\alpha_1,\alpha_2]+PQ=0,\qquad [\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]-PP^\dagger+Q^\dagger Q=0.$$

The second equality is an equality of Hermitian endomorphisms of $V$. It is an algebraic convention from the displayed source equations; it does not by itself assert the full-rank condition on the source's ADHM linear map or an identification with the run's raw moment maps.

current_declaration.statement: Assume AC. Let $E$ be a smooth finite-rank complex vector bundle on a finite-dimensional complex manifold, and let $D''$ be a smooth complex-linear operator from its smooth sections to smooth $E$-valued $(0,1)$-forms satisfying $D''(fs)=\bar\partial f\otimes s+fD''s$. Extend it to bundle-valued forms by the graded Leibniz rule and suppose $(D'')^2=0$. Near every point there is a smooth invertible frame matrix $G$ with $D''G=0$. The changes between these frames are holomorphic, defining a unique holomorphic vector-bundle structure with Dolbeault operator $D''$. A smooth bundle map intertwines two such operators exactly when it is holomorphic for these structures. The construction is local and requires no projective GAGA, coherence or global vanishing theorem.

current_declaration.statement:

$\mathbb R^m$ with its Euclidean metric. For every open cover $\mathcal U$ of

members of $\mathcal V$. Here locally finite means that every point has an
open neighborhood meeting only finitely many members, and the order bound
means the stated pointwise multiplicity bound.

current_declaration.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its metric topology. Define
$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as the filtered colimit of the fixed-cover ordered
Čech cohomology groups over all open covers, and define $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as
the right derived functors of global sections from an injective resolution.
Then the canonical comparison
$$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
is a natural isomorphism for every integer $q\ge0$, compatible with the
identity identification of both degree-zero groups with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$.

current_declaration.title: Fréchet spaces used in analytic coherent cohomology
current_declaration.statement:
A **Fréchet space** over $\mathbb C$ is a complex vector space $E$ with a Hausdorff locally convex vector-space topology generated by a separating countable family of seminorms $(p_n)_{n\ge1}$ and complete for its seminorm uniformity. Explicitly, use the translation-invariant compatible metric
$$d(x,y)=\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-n}\min\{1,p_n(x-y)\},$$
and require that this metric is complete. A seminorm is a function $p:E\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $p(x+y)\le p(x)+p(y)$ and $p(cx)=|c|p(x)$ for $x,y\in E$ and $c\in\mathbb C$; separating means that for $x\ne0$ some $p_n(x)>0$. Locally convex means that every point has a neighborhood basis of convex sets. One may replace the defining family by the increasing family of its finite maxima.

Completeness here always refers to this vector-space uniformity. A sequence is Cauchy for the displayed metric exactly when it is Cauchy for every defining seminorm: each individual metric summand controls that seminorm at sufficiently small distances, and conversely the geometric tail of the metric series plus finitely many seminorm estimates controls the metric. Thus a seminorm-Cauchy series used in the accompanying proofs converges in $E$. The zero vector space is included, with its unique metric. This is the usual complete metrizable locally convex Fréchet convention.

current_declaration.title: Positive incidence geometry for the coupled Penrose transform
current_declaration.design_state: Authored in batch 68; no design section governs this pair.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $S^4={X\in\mathbb R^5:|X|=1}$ have its unit round metric and the orientation which, on the stereographic chart $S^4\setminus\{\infty\}\cong\mathbb R^4$, is $dx_0\wedge dx_1\wedge dx_2\wedge dx_3$. Put $z_1=x_0+ix_1$, $z_2=x_2+ix_3$, and $r^2=|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2$; in these coordinates the metric is $g=4(1+r^2)^{-2}\sum_{\mu=0}^3dx_\mu^2$. Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$, put $Z=\mathbb CP^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, and define $\pi:Z\to\mathbb HP^1=S^4$ by $\pi(\ell)=\ell+j\ell$ for a complex line $\ell\subset\mathbb H^2$. Its fibres are projective lines $L_x\cong\mathbb CP^1$. In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$, the fibre over finite $z=(z_1,z_2)$ is the line

$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,$$

and the fibre over infinity is $L_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Give $Z$ the Fubini–Study metric induced by the standard Hermitian metric on $\mathbb C^4$ and give $\mathcal O_Z(-2)$ its induced Hermitian metric. On the incidence chart $\lambda_1\ne0$, set $t=\lambda_2/\lambda_1$, $\mu_1/\lambda_1=z_1-\bar z_2t$, and $\mu_2/\lambda_1=z_2+\bar z_1t$. The horizontal complex directions of type $(0,1)$ are spanned by

$$H_1=\partial_{\bar z_1}-t\partial_{z_2},\qquad H_2=\partial_{\bar z_2}+t\partial_{z_1};$$

They annihilate the displayed holomorphic coordinates. Together with $\partial_{\bar t}$ they form a direct local frame of $T^{0,1}Z$. Here $H_i$ are the constant-$t$ chart lifts; their projected complex alpha-plane is intrinsic, but this chart splitting is not asserted to be the global metric splitting. Globally let $V^{0,1}=\ker(d\pi)\cap T^{0,1}Z$, and let $H^{0,1}$ be its Fubini–Study orthogonal complement. Its lifts project to the same alpha-planes and may differ from the displayed $H_i$ by vertical components. All global horizontal/vertical form decompositions use this orthogonal splitting; local computations may use the displayed constant-$t$ splitting after retaining the resulting frame and normalization factors. The second projective chart supplies the same alpha-plane at $t=\infty$. The line bundle $\mathcal O_Z(-1)$ is the tautological holomorphic line bundle and $\mathcal O_Z(-2)=\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\otimes2}$.

current_declaration.title: First-order families of positive real linear monads
current_declaration.statement:
Use the dual-number scheme, relative projective-space charts, finite locally free sheaves and twisting sheaves in [[def-dual-numbers-scheme]], [[def-relative-projective-space-standard-charts]], [[def-locally-free-sheaf-finite-rank]] and [[def-twisting-sheaf-proj]], with the inherited AC convention for the twisting-sheaf construction. Let $A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ and equip it with the conjugate-linear involution $\overline{a+b\epsilon}=\bar a+\bar b\epsilon$. Its reduction is the quotient map $A\to\mathbb C$ sending $\epsilon$ to zero. For every $r\in\mathbb R$, the map $\rho_r:A\to A$ fixing $\mathbb C$ and sending $\epsilon$ to $r\epsilon$ preserves this involution.

A **first-order family of positive real linear monads of dimensions $(k,2k+N,k)$** is a three-term complex of locally free sheaves on $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$,
$$\mathcal O(-1)\otimes_A U_A\xrightarrow{\alpha_A}\mathcal O\otimes_A S_A\xrightarrow{\beta_A}\mathcal O(1)\otimes_A U'_A,$$
where $U_A,S_A,U'_A$ are free $A$-modules of ranks $k,2k+N,k$, each map is homogeneous linear in $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)$, $\beta_A\alpha_A=0$, $\alpha_A$ is a locally split injection, $\beta_A$ is a locally split surjection, and $F_A=\ker\beta_A/\operatorname{im}\alpha_A$ is locally free of rank $N$. The two short exact sequences defined by the kernel and image split locally; hence their formation and the middle cohomology commute with reduction $A\to\mathbb C$. The reduced complex is therefore an ordinary linear monad on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$.

The **first-order locally-free/base-change range** used here further requires that $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,F_A)$ is a free $A$-module and reduction identifies it with $H^0(\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C,F_0)$, where $F_0=F_A\otimes_A\mathbb C$. The image in $S_A$ of the map from the four coefficient copies of $U_A$ under $\alpha_A$ is a direct summand and reduces to the corresponding coefficient-image subspace of $S_0$. For each real twistor line $\ell$ in the reduced projective space, the restriction of $F_A$ to $\ell_A=\ell\times_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Spec}A$ is trivial of rank $N$, and reduction identifies its global sections with $H^0(\ell,F_0|_\ell)$. These conditions state the precise global, coefficient-image, and line-section base-change range; no arbitrary analytic family or algebraization assertion is included.

Extend the coordinate map $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ semilinearly using the involution of $A$; its projective action $\sigma$ is an involution and preserves each real twistor line. A **real twistor line** means the projectivization of a $j$-invariant complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$. Equivalently these are the finite lines
$$\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2,\qquad \mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2,\qquad (z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2,$$
together with $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$. Indeed a nonzero vector $v$ and $jv$ are complex-linearly independent because $j^2=-1$; they span the invariant plane. If its $\lambda$ projection is nonzero, that projection and its quaternionic conjugate give an invertible two-by-two matrix with determinant $|\lambda_1|^2+|\lambda_2|^2$, so it has exactly the displayed graph form; if the projection is zero the plane is the $\mu$ plane. Each fixed-line restriction above means the corresponding constant thickening $\ell_A$.

A first-order real structure on the monad is a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian pairing on $F_A$, linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, whose reduction induces a positive-definite Hermitian form on the holomorphic section space of every real line. A unitary framing at infinity is an isometric isomorphism $F_A|_{\ell_\infty}\cong (A\otimes_\mathbb C W)\otimes_A\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$, where $\ell_\infty=\{\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0\}$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ has its standard Hermitian form.

An isomorphism of such families is an $A$-linear chain isomorphism that intertwines the $\sigma$-Hermitian pairings and the framing. No order or positivity is assigned to elements of $A$ with nonzero nilpotent part: positivity is required only after reduction. The base-change scope in this definition consists exactly of reduction $\epsilon\mapsto0$ and the involution-preserving maps $\rho_r$ for real $r$.

current_declaration.title: Chern character and charge normalization of a linear twistor monad
current_declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the named projective-cohomology and characteristic-class suppliers.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal F$ be the locally free algebraic middle cohomology of a linear monad
$$
\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1)^{\oplus k}
$$
on $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$, with exactness at both ends. Let $H_{\rm alg}=c_1^{\rm alg}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in the Chow ring and let $H_{\rm top}=c_1^{\rm top}(\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^3}(1))$ in singular cohomology. The hyperplane cycle map identifies $H_{\rm alg}$ with $H_{\rm top}$; write $H$ for either class in the corresponding formula. The algebraic Chern character is $N-kH_{\rm alg}^2$, the algebraic first Chern class is zero, the algebraic second Chern class is $kH_{\rm alg}^2$, and the algebraic Euler characteristic is $N-2k$. The underlying topological bundle has total Chern class $1+kH_{\rm top}^2$ through degree six and topological Chern character $N-kH_{\rm top}^2$.

Identify $\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C$ with the twistor space of $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ by the quaternionic structure whose invariant lines are the real incidence lines in the positive stereographic coordinates. Let $\pi:\mathbb P^3_\mathbb C\to S^4$ be the resulting fibration, orient each fiber by its complex orientation, orient the base so the incidence chart followed by the fiber orientation gives the complex orientation of $\mathbb P^3$, and let $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ be the positive point class. Then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently, if the underlying topological bundle of $\mathcal F$ is $\pi^*E$ for a rank-$N$ complex bundle $E\to S^4$ with $c_1(E)=0$, then $c_2(E)=ku$ and $\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=k$.

current_declaration.title: Nilpotence of the Finite-Jet Non-Abelian BRST Differential
current_declaration.statement: Let $n\geq 1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, and let $V=V_{\bar 0}\oplus V_{\bar 1}$ be a finite-dimensional graded complex vector space with an even Lie-algebra representation $\rho:\mathfrak g\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$. Form the graded-commutative finite-jet algebra over $C^\infty(U)$ from an even $\mathfrak g$-valued local one-form $A=A_\mu^aT_a\,dx^\mu$, a ghost $c=c^aT_a$ with odd components of ghost number one, and matter fields $\psi^\alpha$ of fixed component parity and ghost number zero. Let $D_\mu$ be the total derivatives on coefficient functions and formal field jets, and let $s$ be the left odd derivation of ghost number one specified by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, $s\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$, and $s(D_I\Phi)=D_I(s\Phi)$ on every multi-index jet. Then $s^2=0$ on the entire finite-jet algebra and $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$ for each $\mu$.

current_declaration.design_state: B-page source-reported ABJM matrix integral with exact one-loop factors, Weyl measure, level sign, real contour, and formal-source limits.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix the adopted zero-mass, zero-Fayet–Iliopoulos ABJM model on the round sphere of radius $r>0$, with $N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}$ and nonzero integer level $k$. Let $s_i,\widehat s_i\in\mathbb R$ be the eigenvalues of the two constant Hermitian Cartan scalars, each of physical dimension $r^{-1}$, and put $\lambda_i=rs_i$ and $\widehat\lambda_i=r\widehat s_i$. In the Kapustin–Willett–Yaakov Euclidean level convention, the source-reported formal localization expression is
$$
Z_{\mathrm{ABJM}}(\mathbb S^3_r)=\frac{1}{(N!)^2}\int_{\mathbb R^{2N}}\left(\prod_{i=1}^N d\lambda_i\,d\widehat\lambda_i\right)e^{-i\pi k\left(\sum_i\lambda_i^2-\sum_i\widehat\lambda_i^2\right)}\frac{\displaystyle\prod_{1\le i<j\le N}\left(2\sinh\!\left(\pi(\lambda_i-\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2\left(2\sinh\!\left(\pi(\widehat\lambda_i-\widehat\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2}{\displaystyle\prod_{i,j=1}^N\left(2\cosh\!\left(\pi(\lambda_i-\widehat\lambda_j)\right)\right)^2}.
$$
Each Cartan variable is integrated over the real line. The integer level and the dimensionless eigenvalues fix every exponent and hyperbolic-function argument; the factor $(N!)^{-2}$ is the inverse order of the two Weyl groups. Mariño's convention uses $\mu_i=2\pi\lambda_i$ and $g_s=2\pi i/k_{\mathrm{Marino}}$; it gives the same displayed phase after setting $k_{\mathrm{Marino}}=-k$. The displayed real-contour expression is oscillatory. It is the source's matrix-integral result under its formal localization and determinant prescriptions, not a construction of the continuum functional measure, a proof of the localization limit, or a formula for every three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ theory.

current_declaration.title: Spectral-network, framed BPS, and defect data in a specified class-S model
current_declaration.design_state: Assigned A-page definition authored from the exact future item contract; its only local item edge is the inspected model-bound defect-insertion definition.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $K\ge2$. A **Riemann surface** here is a connected complex one-manifold; assume $\overline C$ compact. A **selected class-S input of type $A_{K-1}$** consists of $\overline C$, a finite marked set $P\subset\overline C$, a collection $D$ of specified puncture defects at $P$, a Coulomb-branch datum $u=(\phi_2,\ldots,\phi_K)$, a selected global form with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(K)$, and a four-dimensional rigid $\mathcal N=2$ model $\mathcal T$ on $M=\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,+1,+1,+1)$, a chosen orientation, and a chosen time orientation. The model is adopted data: its six-dimensional $\mathcal N=(2,0)$ construction compactifies on $\overline C$ with a specified twist, meaning a chosen background coupling of the six-dimensional internal R-symmetry bundle to the tangent-bundle connection on $\overline C$ for which the compactification is taken to preserve four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ supersymmetry. This definition does not construct a continuum quantum field theory. The selected model also supplies its field bundles, admissible configuration space and field regularity, boundary conditions, observables, normalized correlation functional, and any regulator or measure used; none is deduced here. Put $C=\overline C\setminus P$. The holomorphic cotangent line bundle of $\overline C$ is $K_{\overline C}$. The sections $\phi_r$ of $K_{\overline C}^{\otimes r}$, for $2\le r\le K$, are meromorphic, have poles only in $P$, and have pole orders and residues fixed by $D$. The selected global form and allowed line and surface operators are part of the model data. Thus the coefficients have the units of the corresponding powers of mass when the Seiberg–Witten one-form is assigned mass dimension one. Use $c=\hbar=1$ and retain the model's trace, charge, and central-charge normalizations. A four-dimensional **Bogomolny–Prasad–Sommerfield (BPS) state** is a state in a model-supplied one-particle sector annihilated by a nonzero subset of the model's supercharges; when the selected supersymmetry algebra supplies a massive rest-fiber mass operator $M$ and central charge $Z$, its BPS-saturation condition is $M=|Z|$. No such state or algebraic identification is implied by the geometric data below.

Let $p:T^*\overline C\to\overline C$ be the cotangent-bundle projection and let $\lambda$ be its tautological Liouville one-form. The **spectral curve** $\Sigma_u$ is the compactification of the degree-$K$ curve in $T^*\overline C$ defined by

$$\lambda^K+\sum_{r=2}^{K}p^*\phi_r\,\lambda^{K-r}=0,$$

Write $\pi=p|_{\Sigma_u}:\Sigma_u\to\overline C$ and also use $\lambda$ for the restriction of the tautological one-form. The curve is required to be reduced and to define a finite degree-$K$ branched cover. A **branch point** is a point of $\overline C$ over which at least one point of $\Sigma_u$ has local degree greater than one; the **branch locus** is the set of all such values. Away from the branch locus and $P$, the local roots are one-forms $\lambda^{(1)},\ldots,\lambda^{(K)}$. Remove the poles of $\lambda$ and write $\widetilde\Sigma=\Sigma_u\setminus\operatorname{Pol}(\lambda)$. The geometric charge group is the first singular homology $\Gamma_{\rm geom}=H_1(\widetilde\Sigma;\mathbb Z)$, namely closed integral one-cycles modulo boundaries. For a marked subset $A\subseteq\widetilde\Sigma$, relative one-cycles are chains in $\widetilde\Sigma$ whose boundary lies in $A$, modulo boundaries of two-chains in $\widetilde\Sigma$ and one-chains contained in $A$; their classes form $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A;\mathbb Z)$.

For distinct sheets $i,j$, a regular **$ij$-trajectory of Wentzel–Kramers–Brillouin (WKB) phase** $\vartheta_{\rm W}\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z$ is a $C^1$ immersed path $z:I\to C\setminus\operatorname{Branch}(\pi)$, for an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$, with $\dot z\ne0$ and

$$\operatorname{Im}\!\left(e^{-i\vartheta_{\rm W}}(\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)})(\dot z)\right)=0.$$

Orient it so the real part inside this expression is positive. Reversing the orientation exchanges $ij$ with $ji$. A geometric WKB network is generated from the maximal such trajectories issuing from branch points and from the local junction rule: when compatible $ij$- and $jk$-trajectories meet, an $ik$-trajectory may issue from their joint. A simple branch point is one where exactly two sheets ramify and their local difference is proportional to $z^{1/2}$ in a local coordinate; this square-root form gives three outgoing trajectory directions. A physical **spectral network** also includes the model-supplied soliton data on its walls; in the usual class-S construction an $ij$ wall carries a soliton index $\mu$. A geometric trajectory with no supplied nonzero soliton data is not thereby a physical BPS state. The WKB phase $\vartheta_{\rm W}$ is independent data from the phase $\vartheta_{\rm fr}$ of a supersymmetric interface unless the selected model supplies a relation.

A **finite web** is a finite connected metric ribbon graph: each edge has positive finite length and a cyclic order at each vertex; each internal vertex is trivalent and maps to a network joint, and each external univalent vertex maps to a branch point. The metric is part of the declared convention. In the Gaiotto–Moore–Neitzke (GMN) string convention, an $ij$ edge has length $L_{ij}=\int_a^b |(\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)})(\dot z(t))|\,dt$ along a regular parameterization $z:[a,b]\to C$, and its physical string mass is $L_{ij}/\pi$. In the geometric cubic-differential convention, a lifted T3 edge has flat length $L_{\rm KT}=\int |\lambda(\dot{\tilde z}(t))|\,dt$ on the canonical cover. For a local K=3 sheet pair with $\lambda^{(i)}-\lambda^{(j)}=(1-\omega)\lambda$, the GMN edge length is $\sqrt3 L_{\rm KT}$; these conventions are not silently identified. The graph's map is isometric in the explicitly selected edge metric, with its sheet-pair labels, to compatible network trajectories. Closed edges are permitted. An open web ending at a surface-defect parameter point is instead a relative web. For a closed web, the chosen sheet-lift rule joins its oriented sheetwise edge lifts into a cycle $\gamma_{\rm geom}\in\Gamma_{\rm geom}$. For an open web on a surface defect $\mathbb S_z$, put $A_z=\pi^{-1}(z)\subset\widetilde\Sigma$; its lifted chain is a class in $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A_z;\mathbb Z)$ with boundary $z^{(j)}-z^{(i)}$ for its outgoing $ij$ edge, where $z^{(i)}$ and $z^{(j)}$ are the corresponding preimages of $z$. For an interface path $\wp:z_1\to z_2$, put $A_{12}=\pi^{-1}(\{z_1,z_2\})\subset\widetilde\Sigma$; its framed charge $\bar a$ is a class in $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma,A_{12};\mathbb Z)$ with boundary $z_2^{(j)}-z_1^{(i)}$. These lifts depend on the stated local branch and junction rules. The physical charge group $\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$ is a model-specified quotient of a subgroup $\Gamma_0\le\Gamma_{\rm geom}$, supplied with a surjective quotient map $\rho:\Gamma_0\to\Gamma_{\mathcal T}$; it is not identified with all of $H_1(\widetilde\Sigma;\mathbb Z)$ by notation alone.

For geometric periods use $Z_{\rm geom}(\gamma)=\int_\gamma\lambda$. The physical central charge is a model-supplied function $Z_{\mathcal T}:\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\to\mathbb C$ of mass dimension one. The selected GMN normalization $Z_{\mathcal T}(\rho(\gamma))=\pi^{-1}\int_\gamma\lambda$ for $\gamma\in\Gamma_0$ is available only when $\int_\kappa\lambda=0$ for every $\kappa\in\ker\rho$, so the period formula is independent of the representative of $\rho(\gamma)$. If this descent condition is not supplied, the physical central charge remains a separate model datum and no equality with geometric periods is asserted. A cubic-differential T3 geometry may use $Z_{\rm geom}$; its geometric normalization is not a physical mass normalization.

For a generic point $z\in C$ outside the branch and puncture loci, the selected model may supply a canonical half-BPS surface defect $\mathbb S_z$ in the fundamental representation of the type-$A_{K-1}$ Lie algebra, whose $K$ isolated gapped vacua are labeled by $\pi^{-1}(z)$. It is a codimension-two insertion: model-specified local field, operator, or boundary data are supported on a smooth embedded two-dimensional submanifold of $M$ labeled by $z$; no topological invariance is assumed. In Cartesian coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ one standard interface arrangement places $\mathbb S_{z_1}$ on $x^2=x^3=0$, $x^1<0$, places $\mathbb S_{z_2}$ on $x^2=x^3=0$, $x^1>0$, and places their interface along $x^1=x^2=x^3=0$. A generic interface datum consists of distinct regular points $z_1,z_2$, a path $\wp:z_1\to z_2$, and a phase $\vartheta_{\rm fr}$, giving a half-BPS interface $L_{\wp,\vartheta_{\rm fr}}$ between the two surface defects. In the convention used here, genericity excludes any nonzero bulk or relative central charge on the forbidden ray $e^{-i\vartheta_{\rm fr}}Z\in\mathbb R_{<0}$.

When the indicated one-particle Hilbert sectors and trace domains exist and the traces are trace class, the **bulk second-helicity index** is

$$\Omega_{\mathcal T}(\gamma)=-\frac12\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{\gamma}}\!\left((-1)^{2J_3}(2J_3)^2\right),$$

where $J_3$ is the self-adjoint generator of a massive four-dimensional spatial rotation in the rest frame. The unrefined **surface-defect soliton index** is $\mu(\bar a)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{\mathbb S_z,\bar a}}F e^{i\pi F}$, with $F$ the specified fermion-number operator. The framed index for $L_{\wp,\vartheta_{\rm fr}}$ is

$$\overline\Omega(L_{\wp,\vartheta_{\rm fr}},\bar a;y)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathcal H^{1,\mathrm{BPS}}_{L_{\wp,\vartheta_{\rm fr}},\bar a}} e^{i\pi F}(-y)^{\mathcal J},\qquad \mathcal J=2J_{12}+2I_{12},$$

where $J_{12}$ is the generator of spatial rotations in the selected $1$–$2$ plane, $I_{12}$ is the selected $SU(2)_R$ generator, and $y$ is dimensionless; $y=1$ gives the unrefined framed index in this GMN convention. The choice of fermion-number operator and sign refinement is part of the model data; without it these indices are defined only up to sign. When the chosen sign refinement requires an extended lift of $\bar a$, the index is indexed by that lift and it must not be silently identified with a function of $\bar a$ alone. The cited LNM chapter writes its unrefined framed trace as $\operatorname{Tr} e^{i\pi F}$; these are recorded as separate conventions, with no equality asserted without a supplied operator relation. The geometric network does not determine any of these traces without the specified physical Hilbert sectors.

current_declaration.title: Stable ADHM quotient charts, properness and torus lifts
current_declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard bases. Let $X$ be the stable locus in the complex ADHM equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, where $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$, and stability means that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$. The action $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ of $GL(V)$ on $X$ is free and proper. Its orbit quotient with quotient topology is a Hausdorff second-countable complex manifold of complex dimension $2kN$, with tangent space $\ker d_1/\operatorname{im}d_0$ for the infinitesimal ADHM deformation maps.

For $k>0$, a word frame $C(x)$ is a matrix whose columns are $k$ fixed words in $B_1,B_2$ applied to fixed standard framing basis vectors. The opens $U_C=\{x:\det C(x)\ne0\}$ cover $X$; words of length at most $k-1$ suffice. Each slice $S_C=\{x\in U_C:C(x)=I_V\}$ gives quotient coordinates, with $GL(V)\times S_C\to U_C$ a biholomorphism. Slice changes are holomorphic, in fact given by matrix inversion and polynomial operations on their domains. The quotient is also a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite $T$-invariant affine atlas of these slices, and the map from $X$ is a geometric quotient in the regular-function sense.

Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ act by $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, with $h$ acting on the $\alpha$th standard framing vector by $e_\alpha^{-1}$. This descends to a smooth holomorphic action. At any fixed quotient point represented by $x$, there is a unique $g(t)\in GL(V)$ with $t\cdot x=g(t)\cdot x$. If column $\ell$ of $C(x)$ uses framing color $\alpha_\ell$ and contains $a_\ell,b_\ell$ letters $B_1,B_2$, then

$$g(t)=C(x)\operatorname{diag}(e_{\alpha_\ell}t_1^{a_\ell}t_2^{b_\ell})C(x)^{-1}.$$

Thus the lift is a smooth character representation, without assuming Zariski density or a GIT linearization theorem. For $k=0$ the quotient is a point and these matrices and tangent spaces have their empty-dimensional interpretations. No correspondence with a real moment-map quotient, sheaf moduli or ASD connections is asserted.

current_declaration.title: Entrywise conjugation does not match the raw ADHM real moment map
current_declaration.statement:
Let $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,P,Q)$ obey the source equations stated in the following references section. Under the proposed substitution

$$B_i=\overline{\alpha_i},\qquad I=\overline P,\qquad J=\overline Q,$$

the raw complex moment map vanishes, but the raw real moment map is

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}=\overline C+\overline X-\overline Y,$$

where $C=[\alpha_1,\alpha_1^\dagger]+[\alpha_2,\alpha_2^\dagger]$, $X=PP^\dagger$, and $Y=Q^\dagger Q$. The conjugated source real equation gives $\overline C-\overline X+\overline Y=0$, so on source solutions the proposed raw real moment map equals $2\overline C$; the source equations alone therefore do not establish its vanishing. This failure occurs for the explicit $k=N=2$ source solution in the proof below.

current_declaration.title: Local relations among Weierstrass polynomials reduce to bounded degree
current_declaration.statement: Let $n,q,d\ge1$ be integers, let $U'\subseteq\mathbb C^{n-1}$ and $D\subseteq\mathbb C$ be polydiscs, let $w$ denote the last coordinate, and let $P_1,\ldots,P_q\in\mathcal O(U')[w]$ be monic Weierstrass polynomials with $1\le\deg_w P_j\le d$. For every $x=(x',w_0)\in U'\times D$, each germ in the relation sheaf of $(P_1,\ldots,P_q)$ at $x$ is an $\mathcal O_{U'\times D,x}$-linear combination of relation germs whose components are polynomials in $w-w_0$ of degree at most $d$ with coefficients in $\mathcal O_{U',x'}$.

compact-support cohomology assertion.

current_declaration.title: Presentation and Čech quotient topologies for coherent analytic sections
current_declaration.statement:
Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaf. On an open set $V$ contained in a coordinate chart and in a neighborhood with a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$, where $p_0,p_1$ are finite nonnegative ranks, require that the section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Give $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ the compact-convergence topology generated by the seminorms $f\mapsto\sup_{z\in K}\lVert f(z)\rVert$ for compact $K\subset V$, and give $\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ the quotient topology induced by that surjection. On any open subset covered by countably many such sets, use the topology of the closed subspace of the product of their local section spaces consisting of compatible families. For a finite ordered open cover $\mathcal U=(U_i)$ whose nonempty finite intersections have these section topologies, give each Čech cochain space

$$C^q(\mathcal U,\mathcal F):=\prod_{i_0<\cdots<i_q}\Gamma(U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_q},\mathcal F),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{q+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{q+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{q+1}}\big|_{U_{i_0}\cap\cdots\cap U_{i_{q+1}}}.$$

the finite-product topology, give its cocycle space the subspace topology, and give the quotient of cocycles by coboundaries the Čech quotient topology. current_declaration.title: Exact holomorphic hyperplane sequences for negative twists
current_declaration.statement:
For $r\ge1$, let $H=\{[Z_0:\cdots:Z_r]\in\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C):Z_0=0\}$ and
let $i:H\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^r(\mathbb C)$ be inclusion. For every
integer $m$, the homogeneous coordinate $Z_0$ defines an exact sequence of
holomorphic sheaves
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1)
\xrightarrow{\ \cdot Z_0\ }\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(m)\longrightarrow0.
$$
Here $i_*\mathcal O_H(m)$ assigns to an open set $U$ the holomorphic
sections of $\mathcal O_H(m)$ on $U\cap H$. Twisting the sequence with
$m=0$ by $\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)$ gives, in particular,
$$
0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-2)
\longrightarrow\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(-1)
\longrightarrow i_*\mathcal O_H(-1)\longrightarrow0.
$$

current_declaration.title: Raw monad full rank and ADHM regularity
current_declaration.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, and let $B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, $J:V\to W$ satisfy $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Define for $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$
$$
a_z=(B_1-z_1,\ B_2-z_2,\ J)^T:V\to V\oplus V\oplus W,\qquad
b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,\ B_1-z_1,\ I):V\oplus V\oplus W\to V.
$$
Then $a_z$ is injective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is costable, and $b_z^\dagger$ is surjective for every $z$ if and only if the datum is stable, where stability and costability have their word-span and invariant-subspace meanings. For the homogeneous linear maps
$$
\alpha=(B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\ B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,\ J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,
$$
$$
\beta=(-C,\ A,\ I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2),\quad
A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1,\quad
C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2,
$$
fiberwise injectivity of $\alpha$ and surjectivity of $\beta$ on $\mathbb P^3$ imply regularity. Conversely, if the datum is regular and both raw moment maps vanish, then these homogeneous maps are fiberwise injective and surjective and form a linear bundle monad.

current_declaration.title: Classical BV Antibracket and Yang–Mills Master-Action Data
current_declaration.statement:
Use the local field data and BRST convention on an open set $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ given by a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, a graded representation space $V$, an even $\mathfrak g$-valued gauge potential $A_\mu$, an odd ghost $c$ of ghost number $1$, and matter components $\psi^\alpha$ of parity $\epsilon_\alpha$ and ghost number $0$. For every field or ghost coordinate $\Phi^A$ of parity $\epsilon_A$ and ghost number $g_A$, introduce an antifield $\Phi_A^*$ of parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Thus $A^*$ and the antifields of even matter are odd of ghost number $-1$, while $c^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. The minimal sector consists of $A,\psi,c$ and these antifields.

For a finite-dimensional canonical coordinate algebra, take the polynomial algebra in the even coordinates tensor the exterior algebra in the odd coordinates. In the local-field notation, use finite-jet local functionals with variational derivatives only when the chosen domain makes those derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined; compact support or boundary conditions that kill surface terms are part of that domain. For homogeneous functionals $F,G$, define the canonical antibracket by

$$
(F,G):=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_r F}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right),
$$

with an integral over $U$ replacing the sum in a local-field expression. Left and right derivatives are the graded derivatives acting from the indicated side. This convention has odd parity, ghost number $+1$, the shifted graded-skew identity, the shifted Jacobi identity, and the graded Leibniz identity. A regular finite-dimensional canonical domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number $1$: an element central against every coordinate has all coordinate derivatives zero and is a numerical constant. A formal local-functional domain used below must separately satisfy this same no-ghost-number-one-center condition.

Let a local gauge parameter be a smooth map $\lambda:U\to\mathfrak g$, and define its infinitesimal action on the fields by $\delta_\lambda A_\mu=\partial_\mu\lambda+[A_\mu,\lambda]$ and $\delta_\lambda\psi=-\rho(\lambda)\psi$. Write these variations as $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i=R^i_\alpha[\Phi]\lambda^\alpha$, where $R$ is the resulting linear differential operator in $\lambda$. Assume this declared gauge action is irreducible: if $\delta_\lambda\Phi^i\equiv0$ for every field configuration, then $\lambda\equiv0$. Assume also that its Lie-algebra action closes off shell, meaning its commutator closes without using equations of motion, and that no additional gauge symmetry is included. Let $S_0[A,\psi]$ be a specified local classical action invariant under these transformations. Write $s_0$ for the BRST operator on the minimal fields given by $s_0A_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $s_0c=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s_0\psi=-\rho(c)\psi$. The minimal BV functional candidate is

$$S_{\mathrm{BV}}:=S_0+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*\,s_0\Phi^A,$$

where each product is in the displayed order and the same left/right derivative convention is used in the antibracket. It is a **classical master action** exactly when it satisfies the classical master equation $(S_{\mathrm{BV}},S_{\mathrm{BV}})=0$; the displayed formula alone does not assert that a particular $S_0$ satisfies that equation.

The optional nonminimal sector adds an odd antighost $\bar c^a$ of ghost number $-1$, an even auxiliary field $b^a$ of ghost number $0$, and their antifields, with the BV functional term $-\bar c_a^*b^a$ giving $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. This definition makes no cohomological contractibility claim for that pair. The formal local-field notation does not define an infinite-dimensional measure, a BV Laplacian $\Delta$, a path integral, or the quantum master equation.

current_declaration.title: Local BRST Cohomology Modulo Total Derivatives
current_declaration.statement:
Let $n\geq1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and open, let $\mathcal F_U$ be the finite-jet local algebra with nilpotent BRST derivation $s$ and commuting total derivatives $D_\mu$, and let $dx^1,\ldots,dx^n$ be anticommuting coordinate one-forms. For $g\in\mathbb Z$ and $0\leq p\leq n$, let $\mathcal A_U^{g,p}$ be the space of local horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$, namely finite sums of $dx^{\mu_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge dx^{\mu_p}$ with coefficients in the ghost-number-$g$ part of $\mathcal F_U$. Define the horizontal differential $d_H:=dx^\mu D_\mu$; its square is $d_H^2a=dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu D_\mu D_\nu a=\tfrac12dx^\mu\wedge dx^\nu[D_\mu,D_\nu]a=0$. Extend $s$ to horizontal forms by $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge sa$. Since $sD_\mu=D_\mu s$, one has $s(d_Ha)=-dx^\mu\wedge D_\mu(sa)=-d_H(sa)$, hence $sd_H+d_Hs=0$.

For $p=0$, set $\mathcal A_U^{g,-1}=\{0\}$. The local BRST cohomology modulo total derivatives in bidegree $(g,p)$ is

$$H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H):=\frac{\{a\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p}:\text{there is }b\in\mathcal A_U^{g+1,p-1}\text{ with }sa+d_Hb=0\}}{\{sm+d_Hn:m\in\mathcal A_U^{g-1,p},\ n\in\mathcal A_U^{g,p-1}\}}.$$

The denominator is a subspace of the numerator: for $a=sm+d_Hn$, choose $b=sn$ and compute $sa+d_Hb=s^2m+sd_Hn+d_Hsn=0$. For $p=0$, $n=b=0$ and the same verification reduces to $s^2m=0$. This is cohomology of the specified local jet algebra and horizontal differential; it is not cohomology of a physical state space or Hilbert space. Interpreting $d_H$-exact top forms as equal local functionals additionally assumes compact support or boundary conditions that make the corresponding surface term vanish.

current_declaration.title: Stable ADHM partition fixed points and tangent character
current_declaration.statement:
Assume full AC. Fix integers $N\geq1$ and $k\geq0$ and a positive real stability parameter $\zeta$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ have their standard Hermitian structures. Define $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ to be the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of data $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, $I\in\operatorname{Hom}(W,V)$, $J\in\operatorname{Hom}(V,W)$, $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$, and $\operatorname{span}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ w\in W\}=V$. The positive parameter $\zeta$ specifies the positive-FI stability chamber. Let $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$, with rotation characters $t_1,t_2$ and dual framing characters $e_1,\ldots,e_N$. Thus $W$ has character $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $W^\vee$ has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$. Its action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Work over the rational function field $K=\mathbb Q(\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N)$ in algebraically independent variables. For $\chi=t_1^{m_1}t_2^{m_2}\prod_\alpha e_\alpha^{n_\alpha}$ set $u_\chi=m_1\epsilon_1+m_2\epsilon_2+\sum_\alpha n_\alpha a_\alpha$.

For a partition $Y$, a Young diagram means a finite downward-closed subset of $\mathbb Z_{\geq0}^2$; write $|Y|$ for its number of boxes. For an $N$-tuple $\vec Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_N)$ set $|\vec Y|=\sum_\alpha|Y_\alpha|$, $\mathbf W=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha^{-1}$, $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_\alpha e_\alpha$, and
$$\mathbf V_{\vec Y}=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha\sum_{(i,j)\in Y_\alpha}t_1^it_2^j.$$
Then $\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N}$ is smooth of complex dimension $2kN$, and its $T$-fixed points are isolated and in bijection with the $N$-tuples of partitions of total size $k$. At the fixed point $\vec Y$, the tangent character is
$$\operatorname{ch}_T(T_{\vec Y}\mathcal M^\zeta_{k,N})=\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf V_{\vec Y}(t_1+t_2-1-t_1t_2)+\mathbf V_{\vec Y}^{\vee}\mathbf W^\vee+t_1t_2\mathbf W\mathbf V_{\vec Y}.$$
Let $E_{\vec Y}$ be the product of $u_\chi$ over the tangent weights counted with multiplicity; the fixed points are isolated, so none of these weights is zero. Define the fixed-point series by
$$Z^{\mathrm{fp}}_N(q)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k\sum_{|\vec Y|=k}E_{\vec Y}^{-1}\in K\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
Each coefficient is a finite sum, and the series is formal; no analytic convergence is asserted.

The quotient is a separated smooth finite-type complex algebraic variety with a finite invariant affine word-slice atlas for the algebraic complex torus $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^*)^{N+2}$. This result concerns the stable matrix quotient and a formal series. It asserts no sheaf/ASD dictionary or integration identity.

current_declaration.title: Real and complex ADHM quotients at positive and regular zero FI
current_declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, standard Hermitian $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$ and ADHM data $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with the complex equation $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Stability means that the $B_1,B_2$ words applied to $I(W)$ span $V$; costability means no nonzero common invariant subspace of $V$ lies in $\ker J$; regular means both. Set

$$\mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

For every $\zeta>0$, each stable $GL(V)$ orbit meets $\mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V$ in exactly one $U(V)$ orbit, and the inclusion induces a diffeomorphism of smooth real manifolds

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta I_V,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^s/GL(V).$$

At $\zeta=0$, every stable datum satisfying the real equation is automatically costable. Each regular complex orbit meets the zero real level in exactly one unitary orbit, giving instead

$$\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=0,\ \mathrm{stable}\}/U(V)\ \cong\ X^{\mathrm{reg}}/GL(V).$$

Both identifications are equivariant for the compact rotation/framing torus in the raw-data convention. For $k=0$ all spaces are points. This theorem identifies the stated finite-dimensional quotients; it asserts no correspondence with sheaves or ASD connections, and no identification of the entire positive-FI quotient with the zero-FI regular locus.

current_declaration.title: Oka coherence and local coherent free resolutions
current_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold and let $\mathcal O_M$ be its sheaf of holomorphic functions. For every open $U\subseteq M$ and every finite tuple $f_1,\ldots,f_q\in\mathcal O_M(U)$, the relation sheaf
$$
\ker\!\left(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus q}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_U,\quad(a_1,\ldots,a_q)\longmapsto\sum_{j=1}^q a_jf_j\right)
$$
is locally of finite type: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite family of relation sections generates the relation stalk at every point. Consequently $\mathcal O_M$ is coherent. Coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module sheaves are closed under kernels, cokernels, and finite extensions. For every coherent $\mathcal O_M$-module $\mathcal F$, point $x\in M$, and finite integer $\ell\ge0$, there are a chart neighborhood $W$ of $x$ and finite ranks $p_0,\ldots,p_\ell$ for which
$$
\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\mathcal O_W^{\oplus p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0
$$
is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except the leftmost one. No exactness at the leftmost free term and no global analytic free resolution are asserted.

Stalk Noetherianity alone is insufficient.

current_declaration.title: Schwartz compact-perturbation theorem for Fréchet spaces
current_declaration.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $E$ and $F$ be Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$. A continuous linear map $g:E\to F$ is called a quasi-epimorphism when its image is closed and has finite codimension in $F$. A continuous linear map $h:E\to F$ is called compact when the image of some neighborhood of $0$ has compact closure in $F$. If $g$ is a quasi-epimorphism and $h$ is compact, then $g+h:E\to F$ is a quasi-epimorphism.

current_declaration.title: Canonical Antibracket Generates the Declared BRST Field Variations
current_declaration.statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be the finite-dimensional algebra that is polynomial in even canonical coordinates and exterior in odd canonical coordinates $\Phi^A,\Phi_A^*$. Give each homogeneous minimal coordinate $\Phi^A$ parity $\epsilon_A\in\{0,1\}$ and ghost number $g_A$, and give its antifield parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $-1-g_A$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$ (F,G)=\sum_A\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi^A}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi_A^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial\Phi_A^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial\Phi^A}\right). $$

Suppose each $s_0\Phi^A$ is independent of all antifields, has parity $\epsilon_A+1\pmod 2$ and ghost number $g_A+1$, and let $S_0$ be even of ghost number zero and independent of antifields. Define $S:=S_0+\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*s_0\Phi^A$, with the displayed product order. Then $(S,\Phi^A)=s_0\Phi^A$ for each minimal coordinate. For a local-field version on a nonempty open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, use fields $\Phi^A(x)$ and antifields $\Phi_A^*(x)$ with the same parity and ghost-number assignments, replace coordinate derivatives in the bracket by variational derivatives and the sum by $\int_U d^nx$, and set $S_U:=S_{0,U}+\int_U d^nx\,\sum_A(-1)^{\epsilon_A}\Phi_A^*(x)s_0\Phi^A(x)$. If this domain makes the variational derivatives and integrations by parts well-defined and its boundary term vanishes, then $(S_U,\Phi^A(x))=s_0\Phi^A(x)$ pointwise.

current_declaration.title: Framed U(N) Instanton Moduli and ADHM Data
current_declaration.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $N\geq 2$ and let $S^4=\mathbb R^4\cup\{\infty\}$ be the one-point compactification, oriented so the coordinates $x^1,x^2,x^3,x^4$ on $\mathbb R^4$ have $dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3\wedge dx^4>0$. Give $S^4$ a smooth round metric in the conformal class of the Euclidean metric on $\mathbb R^4$. A framed $U(N)$ connection is a smooth unitary connection $A$ on a Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle $E\to S^4$, together with a chosen unitary frame $\Phi:E_\infty\to\mathbb C^N$ of its fiber at $\infty$. Gauge transformations are smooth unitary bundle automorphisms that equal the identity in this frame at $\infty$. The curvature is $F_A$, and the Hodge operator is defined by $\alpha\wedge *_g\beta=\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle_g\,d\mathrm{vol}_g$ on two-forms. Set $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2$ and $F_A^-=(F_A-*_gF_A)/2$; the anti-self-dual condition is $F_A^+=0$, and the self-dual condition is $F_A^-=0$.

Let $\mathfrak u(N)$ be the anti-Hermitian matrices and put $B_N(X,Y)=-\operatorname{tr}_N(XY)$. In the trace convention of the library, the charge of $A$ is $q_N(A)=(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}B_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$, and the positive anti-self-dual instanton number is $k(A)=-q_N(A)$. For $k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}$, the framed anti-self-dual charge-$k$ moduli set $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ consists of framed pairs $(E,A)$ with $F_A^+=0$ and $k(A)=k$, modulo the stated based gauge transformations. The integer-charge condition is part of the selected bundle sector; no analytic existence or uniqueness assertion is included in this definition. The trace and Hodge conventions agree with the supplied compact-four-manifold definition of $q_B$; its special $SU(2)$ integrality clause is not used to assert $U(N)$ integrality.

For $k\geq0$, take Hermitian spaces $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$. The ADHM data are
$$B_1,B_2\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad I\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V),\qquad J\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W).$$
Their data space is $\mathcal R_{k,N}=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)^2\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(W,V)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb C}(V,W)$, and their complex and real moment-map expressions are
$$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V),\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V).$$
Here $[X,Y]=XY-YX$, and $\dagger$ is the Hermitian adjoint. The two displayed formulas define maps $\mu_{\mathbb C}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ and $\mu_{\mathbb R}:\mathcal R_{k,N}\to\operatorname{Herm}(V)$, where $\mathcal R_{k,N}$ is the stated product of four Hom spaces and $\operatorname{Herm}(V)$ is the real vector space of Hermitian endomorphisms. They are the complex and real ADHM moment-map expressions, with these formulas fixing their normalization. A datum is stable when
$$\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb C}\{B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w):m\geq0,\ i_j\in\{1,2\},\ w\in W\}=V,$$
where the word of length zero is the identity. Equivalently, no proper $B_1,B_2$-invariant subspace of $V$ contains $\operatorname{im}I$. The group $GL(V)$ consists of invertible complex-linear endomorphisms, and $U(V)$ is its subgroup preserving the chosen Hermitian inner product. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$. For $\zeta>0$, the stable complex ADHM quotient $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{GIT},\zeta}_{k,N}$ is the geometric quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $GL(V)$ in the positive stability chamber; $\zeta$ labels that chamber and is not an additional coordinate on the complex equation set.

For a real parameter $\zeta\geq0$, the real moment-map presentation is the quotient of $\{\mu_{\mathbb C}=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}=\zeta\,\mathrm{id}_V,\ \text{stable}\}$ by $U(V)$. At $\zeta>0$ this is called the resolved or positive-FI ADHM quotient; at $\zeta=0$ its affine completion includes the small-instanton locus. The equations and quotient are definitions; this item does not assert that the real moment-map quotient is isomorphic to the stable complex quotient or to an instanton moduli space.

Write $\mathbb{CP}^2$ for the complex projective plane, $\ell_\infty=\{[0:z_1:z_2]\}$ for its line at infinity, and $\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ for the sheaf of holomorphic functions on that line. The affine chart $\mathbb{CP}^2\setminus\ell_\infty$ is $\mathbb C^2$; projective compactification adds the whole line $\ell_\infty$, unlike the one-point compactification $S^4$. Let $\mathcal O(1)$ be the hyperplane line bundle and $\mathcal O(m)=\mathcal O(1)^{\otimes m}$ for $m\geq0$. A coherent sheaf is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$-modules that is locally finitely presented; it is torsion-free when no nonzero local section is annihilated by a nonzero local function. Its rank is the dimension of its generic fiber over the function field. Define its Hilbert polynomial by $P_E(m)=\sum_{i=0}^2(-1)^i\dim_{\mathbb C}H^i(\mathbb{CP}^2,E\otimes\mathcal O(m))$ for all sufficiently large integers $m$. The framed Gieseker moduli space $\mathcal G_{k,N}$ is the moduli of pairs $(E,\Phi)$ with $E$ a rank-$N$ torsion-free coherent sheaf, $P_E(m)=N\binom{m+2}{2}-k$, and $\Phi:E|_{\ell_\infty}\cong\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}^{\oplus N}$. Its locally-free locus is distinguished from the boundary of non-locally-free sheaves. The Uhlenbeck set-theoretic compactification is the disjoint union of strata $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k-\ell,N}\times\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)$ for $0\leq\ell\leq k$, where $\operatorname{Sym}^{\ell}(\mathbb R^4)=(\mathbb R^4)^\ell/S_\ell$ records ideal point defects. The Gieseker space and the Uhlenbeck space are distinct: the former retains torsion-free sheaf data at the small-instanton boundary, while the latter records only ideal points. No compactness of either full space is asserted here.

Write $z_1=x^1+ix^2$ and $z_2=x^3+ix^4$. The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times T_G$, with $T_G\subset U(W)$ the diagonal framing torus, acts on ADHM data by
$$(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ).$$
This convention makes $\mu_{\mathbb C}$ transform with character $t_1t_2$ and leaves $\mu_{\mathbb R}$ invariant. Let $e_\alpha$ denote the character of the dual of the $\alpha$th framing line, so the framing representation has character $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and its dual has character $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. current_declaration.title: A Finite Orbit with Two Gauge-Condition Intersections
current_declaration.physical_scope: A finite-dimensional regulated gauge-orbit example only; it is not a non-Abelian Yang–Mills field theory or a continuum functional measure.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $X=\mathbb R^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$ have positive density $|dx\,dy|$, and let $K=S^1$ have angle coordinate $\theta$ and right-invariant density $|d\theta|$. Let $K$ act on the right by
$$(x,y)\cdot e^{i\theta}=(x\cos\theta-y\sin\theta,x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).$$
For $r>0$, set $s_r=(r,0)$, choose an open neighborhood $U_r\subset\{x>0\}$ of $s_r$, let $S_r=U_r\cap\{y=0\}$ have density $|dx|$, and set $\chi(x,y)=y$ on $U_r$. The unit angular generator $1\in\mathfrak k=T_eK\cong\mathbb R$ has infinitesimal orbit vector
$$R_{s_r}(1):=\left.\frac{d}{d\theta}\right|_{0}(s_r\cdot e^{i\theta})=(0,r).$$
The Faddeev–Popov operator is the linear map $M_{s_r}:=d\chi_{s_r}\circ R_{s_r}:\mathfrak k\to\mathbb R$, and its density Jacobian relative to $|d\theta|$ and $|dy|$ is $\Delta_{\rm FP}(s_r)=|\det M_{s_r}|=r>0$. The full orbit $K\cdot s_r$ nevertheless meets the global condition $y=0$ at both $(r,0)$ and $(-r,0)$. Thus the local nonzero Jacobian proves transversality near $s_r$ but does not select one global representative for the orbit. The regulator group $K$ in this finite-dimensional toy is not identified with the model's non-Abelian structure group $G$.

current_declaration.title: Local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly modulo counterterms
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix a four-dimensional smooth spacetime region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with a stated orientation, spin structure, boundary conditions, and unit system. A selected model specifies a continuous global symmetry group $H$, its action on the fields and observables, the nondynamical background connections, the field and jet domains, a regulator and measure or formal perturbative generating functional, and the admissible local counterterms. A background connection is nondynamical model data: it transforms under local changes of background trivialization but is not integrated over.

Let $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{g,p}$ be the finite-jet horizontal $p$-forms of ghost number $g$ generated by the nondynamical background connections and their BRST ghost jets, without matter-field jets, and restrict the model’s nilpotent BRST differential $s$ and horizontal exterior derivative $d_H$ to this background subalgebra. An infinitesimal local anomaly representative is a local horizontal four-form $a_4\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{1,4}$ such that $sa_4+d_Hb_3=0$ for some $b_3\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{bg},U}^{2,3}$. The **local perturbative ’t Hooft anomaly** of the specified global symmetry is the class $[a_4]$ in the relative cohomology $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$ of this background subalgebra, with the quotient taken using exactly the model’s admissible four-dimensional background counterterms and total-derivative boundary convention. Its class is zero exactly when an admissible local counterterm removes the infinitesimal background variation modulo a boundary term.

Any prescribed noninvariance of the classical action or selected couplings is an explicit-symmetry-breaking insertion and is separated before assigning this quantum anomaly class. It is not, by itself, a measure anomaly. A claim of anomaly matching therefore assumes the stated classical symmetry, or carries such breaking insertions separately.

This definition applies to a global symmetry whose background is nondynamical. If the same local class concerns a field integrated over as a gauge redundancy, it is a local gauge anomaly, not a ’t Hooft anomaly; an uncancelled gauge anomaly obstructs the proposed gauging unless a separately specified cancellation mechanism is included. The definition addresses only infinitesimal transformations and makes no claim about large or disconnected transformations, determinant-line holonomy, torsion phases, or a physical continuum limit.

current_declaration.title: Zero-FI regular ADHM and framed twistor data
current_declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with their standard Hermitian inner products. A raw framed ADHM datum is $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$. Its complex and real moment expressions are

$$\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=[B_1,B_2]+IJ,\qquad \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J.$$

The datum is stable when the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$, for $m\geq0$, $i_j\in\{1,2\}$, and $w\in W$, span $V$. It is costable when no nonzero subspace of $V$ is invariant under both $B_1,B_2$ and contained in $\ker J$. It is regular when it is both stable and costable. The group $GL(V)$ acts by $g\cdot x=(gB_1g^{-1},gB_2g^{-1},gI,Jg^{-1})$ and its unitary subgroup is $U(V)$. The regular zero-FI real quotient is the orbit set

$$\mathcal A^{\mathrm{reg}}_{k,N}=\{x:\mu_{\mathbb C}(x)=0,\ \mu_{\mathbb R}(x)=0,\ x\text{ stable and costable}\}/U(V).$$

Let $S^4=\mathbb H\mathbb P^1$ have the unit round metric and the orientation whose restriction to the stereographic coordinates $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$ on $\mathbb R^4=S^4\setminus\{\infty\}$ is $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. For a smooth right principal $U(N)$-bundle $P\to S^4$, let $E=P\times_{U(N)}\mathbb C^N$ be its Hermitian associated vector bundle, let $A$ be a smooth unitary connection, and let $\Phi:E|_{\infty}\to\mathbb C^N$ be a unitary framing. Write $F_A$ for the anti-Hermitian curvature matrix and define

$$q_N(P,A)=-\frac{1}{8\pi^2}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The anti-self-dual equation is $F_A^+=(F_A+*_gF_A)/2=0$. For integer $k\geq0$, the framed ASD sector $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{ASD}}_{k,N}$ is the set of such framed connections satisfying $F_A^+=0$ and $q_N(P,A)=-k$, modulo smooth unitary gauge transformations whose value at $\infty$ is the identity in the framing. This definition alone does not assert that every sector exists or that $q_N$ is integral; the exact $U(N)$ charge normalization is a separate lemma below.

Identify $\mathbb H^2$ with $\mathbb C^4$ using a fixed right quaternionic structure $j$ with $j^2=-1$. The twistor space is $Z=\mathbb C\mathbb P^3=\mathbb P_{\mathbb C}(\mathbb H^2)$, the projection $\pi:Z\to\mathbb H\mathbb P^1=S^4$ sends a complex line $\ell$ to the quaternionic line $\ell+j\ell$, and the antiholomorphic involution is $\sigma([v])=[jv]$. A real twistor line is a fibre $L_x=\pi^{-1}(x)\cong\mathbb C\mathbb P^1$; $\sigma$ restricts to the antipodal map on each such line. Fix homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ so $\sigma$ is induced by $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)\mapsto(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. The finite real line over $z$ has equations $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. These equations fix the quaternionic identification and its orientation. In the chart $\lambda_1=1,\lambda_2=0$, vertical complex orientation followed by the positive orientation of $(z_1,z_2)$ is the complex orientation of $Z$.


For the spinor convention, use the standard spin structure on $S^4$ and $\operatorname{Spin}(4)\cong SU(2)_+\times SU(2)_-$. Let $S^+,S^-$ be the associated rank-two complex spinor bundles, so $T_{\mathbb C}S^4\cong S^+\otimes S^-$. The twistor fibre at $x$ is $\mathbb P(S_x^+)$, and the complex two-plane associated with $\ell\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ is $\ell\otimes S_x^-$. Use the Levi-Civita connection of the round metric for the horizontal distribution of $\pi$; the horizontal $(0,1)$ subspace at $[\ell]\in L_x$ projects to this complex alpha-plane. The displayed orientation is the twistor orientation: the vertical complex orientation followed by the quotient orientation on $S^4$ agrees with the complex orientation on $Z$. It is chosen so the curvature component that vanishes on every such plane is precisely $F^+=(F+*_gF)/2$. In spinor components, $F_{AB}=F_{(AB)}$ denotes the symmetric spinor corresponding to $F^+$ under $\Lambda^2_+T_x^*S^4\otimes\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Sym}^2(S_x^+)^*$; restriction to the plane is $F_{AB}\pi^A\pi^B$, which vanishes for every $[\pi]\in\mathbb P(S_x^+)$ exactly when $F^+=0$.

A linear monad on $Z$ is a complex of holomorphic bundles

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_Z\otimes K\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal O_Z(1)\otimes U',$$

where $U,U',K$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces, $b\circ a=0$, $a$ is injective as a sheaf map, $b$ is surjective, and the cohomology sheaf $\ker b/\operatorname{im}a$ is locally free. It is framed when that cohomology has a specified unitary trivialization on $L_\infty$. For a holomorphic bundle $\mathcal E$ on $Z$ that is holomorphically trivial on every real line, a positive Hermitian Ward reality datum is a holomorphic nondegenerate pairing $b:\mathcal E\otimes\sigma^*\overline{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal O_Z$ satisfying $b_{\sigma z}(v,u)=\overline{b_z(u,v)}$. Here $b_z$ is complex linear in $u\in\mathcal E_z$ and conjugate linear in $v\in\mathcal E_{\sigma z}$; the conjugate pullback is holomorphic because $\sigma$ is antiholomorphic. For holomorphic sections $s,t$ on $L_x$, the function $b_z(s(z),t(\sigma z))$ is holomorphic on the compact line, hence constant. It defines $h_x(s,t)$; require this Hermitian form to be positive definite for every $x$. The metric on each fibre of $\mathcal E|_{L_x}$ is transported from this form by holomorphic evaluation. Thus positive forms are induced by the pairing, not independent arbitrary choices. A framed Ward bundle includes a unitary framing on $L_\infty$ for this induced form. Smoothness and parallelness of the induced section-bundle metric are conclusions of the Ward construction.

The compact torus $T=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ acts on $\mathbb R^4\cong\mathbb C^2$ by $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(t_1z_1,t_2z_2)$ and on $W$ by $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_1^{-1},\ldots,e_N^{-1})$. Its raw ADHM action is

$$ (t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ). $$

On the framed ASD sector, the same torus acts by inverse pullback under the indicated rotation of $S^4$ and by postcomposition of the framing with $h$. On $Z$, the rotations act by $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]\mapsto[\lambda_1:t_1t_2\lambda_2:t_1\mu_1:t_2\mu_2]$, equivalently the projective spin lift to $\mathbb P(S^+)$; the central sign in the spin double cover acts trivially after projectivization, and the induced action commutes with $\sigma$. The framing torus acts on the framed monad cohomology by the same diagonal representation.

with $r_j>0$ and $|a_j|<r_j$ for every $j$. Its coordinate discs need not be
centered at $0$. Define
$$H_D=D\cap\{z_1=0\},\qquad i:H_D\hookrightarrow D,$$
and set $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_D/(z_1)\mathcal O_D$. Then $\mathcal Q$ is
coherent and restriction to the hyperplane induces an isomorphism
$$\mathcal Q\cong i_*\mathcal O_{H_D}.$$
The multiplication sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_D\xrightarrow{\ \cdot z_1\ }\mathcal O_D\longrightarrow\mathcal Q\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, and
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)\cong\mathcal O(H_D),\qquad H^q(D,\mathcal Q)=0\quad(q>0).$$
In particular the global sections are the actual quotient
$\mathcal O(D)/z_1\mathcal O(D)$, identified with holomorphic functions on
$H_D$. All cohomology here is ordinary derived global-sections cohomology;
no small-neighborhood restriction or general coherent Stein vanishing is assumed.

current_declaration.title: Compact morphisms of Fréchet complexes have finite Hausdorff cohomology
current_declaration.statement: Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $(E^\bullet,d)$ and $(F^\bullet,\delta)$ be cochain complexes of Fréchet spaces over $\mathbb C$, with continuous differentials, and let $\rho^\bullet:E^\bullet\to F^\bullet$ be a continuous cochain map. Fix $q\ge0$. If $\rho^q:E^q\to F^q$ is compact and the induced map $H^q(\rho^\bullet):H^q(E^\bullet)\to H^q(F^\bullet)$ is surjective, then $H^q(F^\bullet)$, with its cocycle-subspace and coboundary-quotient topology, is Hausdorff and finite-dimensional. Moreover, whenever a continuous cochain map between Fréchet complexes induces a surjection on $q$th cohomology, that cohomology map is open.
