current_declaration.title: Scalar structure-sheaf cohomology of $\mathbb P^2$
current_declaration.statement:
Assume full AC and let $X$ be the complex lines in $\mathbb C^3$, equivalently
$X=\mathbb P^2(\mathbb C)=(\mathbb C^3\setminus\{0\})/\mathbb C^\times$.
Use the standard charts $U_i=\{[Z_0:Z_1:Z_2]:Z_i\ne0\}$ for $i=0,1,2$,
ordered $0<1<2$. Let $\mathcal O_X$ be the sheaf of holomorphic functions on
$X$. For each nonempty $I\subseteq\{0,1,2\}$ set
$U_I=\bigcap_{i\in I}U_i$ and define
$$C^p=\prod_{|I|=p+1}\mathcal O_X(U_I)\quad(0\le p\le2),\qquad (\delta c)_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}=\sum_{\nu=0}^{p+1}(-1)^\nu c_{i_0\cdots\widehat{i_\nu}\cdots i_{p+1}}|_{U_{i_0\cdots i_{p+1}}},$$
with increasing indices, and $C^p=0$ for $p<0$ or $p>2$; Čech cohomology
means the cohomology of this complex.
For $m=(m_0,m_1,m_2)\in\mathbb Z^3$ with
$m_0+m_1+m_2=0$, write $N(m)=\{i:m_i<0\}$ and call the degree-zero
homogeneous Laurent monomial the mode $m$; in frame $e_i^{(0)}$ its coefficient
is $\prod_{j\ne i}(Z_j/Z_i)^{m_j}$. A mode occurs in the Čech component on
$U_I$ exactly when $N(m)\subseteq I$. The zero mode contributes one copy of
$\mathbb C$ in degree zero, every nonzero mode contracts, and therefore
$$H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)=0\quad(q>0).$$
The contraction is the ordered three-chart Laurent calculation and its
subseries converge locally uniformly on every output intersection.
For $0\le q\le2$, let $\mathcal A_X^{0,q}$ be the sheaf of smooth
antiholomorphic $q$-forms, with differential the $\bar\partial$ part of the
exterior derivative, and set the terms to zero for $q>2$. The same groups are
the cohomology of the global complex $\Gamma(X,\mathcal A_X^{0,\bullet})$ by
the canonical projective Dolbeault comparison.

current_declaration.title: SO(2) orbit with two slice intersections and a stabilizer at the origin
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 draft authored; item readiness is recorded separately. The planned Singer theorem has no carrier and remains explicitly escalated in batch evidence.
current_declaration.statement:
Take $M=\{\star\}$, $G=SU(2)$ as the noncommutative group of unit quaternions, $P=SU(2)\to M$ with right multiplication, $H=0$, and connection form $\omega=q^{-1}dq$. This is an admissible non-Abelian bundle and connection datum. Choose the independent regulator $X=\mathbb R^2$ with Lebesgue density. Write $R_\theta\in SO(2)$ for rotation through angle $\theta$ modulo $2\pi$. Let $K=SO(2)$ with left-invariant density $|d\theta|$, and define the smooth right action
$$
(x,y)\cdot R_\theta=(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta,\,-x\sin\theta+y\cos\theta).
$$
Take $S=\{(x,0):x\in\mathbb R\}$, $\chi(x,y)=y$, and density $dx$ on $S$. At $s=(r,0)$, the orbit differential in the angle direction is $(0,-r)$, so $M_s(1)=-r$ and $\Delta_{\mathrm{FP}}(s)=|r|$. For $r>0$, the orbit-to-slice map is $\Psi(R_\theta,(r,0))=(r\cos\theta,-r\sin\theta)$, whose coordinate Jacobian at the identity is $r$, agreeing with the Faddeev–Popov density ratio. For a fixed orbit point $x_0=(r,0)$, $r>0$, the gauge function is $F_{x_0}(R_\theta)=-r\sin\theta$. Its two zeros are $\theta=0,\pi$, with distinct slice points $(r,0)$ and $(-r,0)$, and both are transverse. Taking $\Gamma=SO(2)$ and the test function $\varphi=1$, the regularized intersection expression tends to $2$. At the origin the full group stabilizes the point, $M_{(0,0)}=0$, and $F_{(0,0)}$ vanishes on all of $SO(2)$; the theorem's isolated transverse-zero hypotheses fail there.

Form the finite graded-commutative coordinate algebra $\mathcal B=\mathbb C[c_1^*,c_2^*,c_3^*]\otimes\Lambda(c^1,c^2,c^3)$, where each $c^a$ is odd of ghost number $1$ and each $c_a^*$ is even of ghost number $-2$. Use the canonical antibracket

$$
(F,G)=\sum_{a=1}^3\left(\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c^a}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c_a^*}-\frac{\partial_rF}{\partial c_a^*}\frac{\partial_lG}{\partial c^a}\right).
$$

For $S_{\mathrm{CE}}=\tfrac12c_a^*\epsilon^a{}_{bc}c^bc^c$, the element $S_{\mathrm{CE}}$ is even with ghost number zero and satisfies $(S_{\mathrm{CE}},S_{\mathrm{CE}})=0$. Hence the Hamiltonian differential $sF=(S_{\mathrm{CE}},F)$ is nilpotent. This is only the finite-dimensional non-Abelian ghost sector; it is not a Yang–Mills action or a quantum field theory.

current_declaration.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise gauge fixing and local renormalization data for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills model; it constructs no continuum functional measure or continuum theory.
current_declaration.statement:
Use the adopted pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model: $G=SU(2)$, $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{su}(2)$, the selected smooth right-principal bundle sector has no matter fields, and the positive invariant form is $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$ for $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. Work in a nonempty local trivialization chart of the selected bundle over oriented, time-oriented Minkowski space with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and coordinates $x^0=t$ in natural units $c=\hbar=1$. With the alternating wedge–Lie bracket fixed by the principal-curvature supplier, write $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted Lorentzian gauge action is $S_0[A]=-(2g_{\rm YM}^2)^{-1}\int\kappa(F_A\wedge *F_A)$, with fixed positive dimensionless $g_{\rm YM}$. In the perturbative formulas $A_\mu$ has canonical engineering dimension $1$ and $g_{\rm YM}$ dimension $0$ in mass units; the ghost $c$ has dimension $0$, the antighost $\bar c$ and auxiliary field $b$ have dimension $2$, and the BRST differential has dimension $0$. Assign each antifield the dimension making its product with the corresponding BRST variation have density dimension $4$. The model postulate supplies the physical units, bundle sector, action, and boundary conditions; the classical gauge-invariance result supplies invariance under the declared bundle gauge transformations. This definition does not prove either supplier.

In the chosen local trivialization write $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and choose the linear covariant gauge condition $G(A)=\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with gauge parameter $\xi>0$. The nonminimal BRST variables are an odd antighost $\bar c$ of ghost number $-1$ and an even auxiliary field $b$ of ghost number $0$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. The gauge-fixing fermion and gauge-fixing contribution are

$$\Psi_\xi=\int d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Here $s$ is the odd BRST derivation on the finite-jet field algebra, extended to the nonminimal variables and their antifields using the specified BV convention. The gauge condition is a local perturbative choice; it does not assert a global slice or remove all gauge copies. A finite-dimensional regulated configuration space has an ordinary Faddeev–Popov Jacobian only when it supplies the finite-dimensional group action, gauge condition, and transverse slice data in the preceding finite-dimensional definition. Such a Jacobian is not a continuum functional determinant and does not define a continuum measure.

A **formal perturbative renormalization datum** consists of the selected pure SU(2) classical BV action $\Gamma_0$, the above gauge-fixing choice, the dimensional-regularization prescription $D=4-2\epsilon$, modified minimal subtraction of the $1/\epsilon$ poles together with $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$, and a local counterterm space $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$. Here $d_*$ is a finite engineering-dimension bound fixed by the selected power-counting prescription; $\mathcal C_{\leq d_*}$ consists of integrated Lorentz-scalar polynomials of ghost number zero and engineering dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and finitely many spacetime derivatives. The usual renormalizable four-dimensional Yang–Mills choice is $d_*=4$. The minimal BV action is the extension of $S_0$ by the antifield couplings to $sA_\mu=D_\mu c$ and $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$; when the nonminimal pair is included it also has the term $-\int_U\bar c^*b$. The datum is admissible only when $\Gamma_0$ satisfies the classical master equation and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. Its loop-counting variable $\lambda$ is formal and dimensionless; a formal effective action is a coefficient sequence $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ and no convergence at any nonzero $\lambda$ is asserted.

For a local BV functional $\Gamma$, define the Slavnov functional by $\mathfrak S(\Gamma):=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$ using the chosen odd antibracket, and define the linearized operator $B_{\Gamma_0}X:=(\Gamma_0,X)$. The datum has the **local QAP property** when, at each first order $n$ where the coefficientwise Slavnov identity fails, its defect has a finite-jet local four-form representative $\delta_n$ of ghost number one and a finite-jet local three-form $\rho_n$ of ghost number two satisfying

$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0.$$

This local representative and consistency condition are part of the QAP input; take $\delta_n$ to have engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and $\rho_n$ at most $d_*-1$. The definition does not prove the QAP. The finite-jet local BRST cohomology $H^{g,p}(s\mid d_H)$ uses the local forms, ghost grading, and horizontal differential of the preceding cohomology definition; $d_H$-exact top forms are identified with zero only under the declared compact-support or boundary condition. The coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identity is $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda))=0$ as an equality of formal power series.

current_declaration.title: Flat-space chiral anomaly-matching data and regulator convention
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
current_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and flat oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and its standard spin structure. Fix Dirac matrices by $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$ and $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$; set $P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2$ and $P_-=I-P_+$. The global symmetry group is the fixed global form $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, acting on a finite multiset $S$ of massless positive-chirality Weyl fields. Each field is a Grassmann-odd smooth compactly supported section of $\operatorname{im}(P_+)\otimes V_i$, where $V_i$ carries a specified finite-dimensional unitary representation $R_i$ of $H$. The chiral kinetic operator is $\mathcal D_{+,i}=P_-i\gamma^\mu D_{\mu,i}P_+$ from positive to negative chirality; its regulated determinant phase is a formal perturbative input. The matter field has mass dimension $3/2$; the background potentials have mass dimension one, their curvature two-forms dimension two, and all $U(1)_V$ charges and trace coefficients are dimensionless. The backgrounds are global one-forms on the trivial bundles over $M$, vary smoothly, and have compact support; the global symmetry is not integrated over as a dynamical gauge redundancy.

For each species, the background covariant derivative is $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+\rho_{i*}(A_\mu,iB_\mu)$ in its representation, where $A$ is an anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection, $B$ is a real $U(1)_V$ connection, and $\rho_{i*}:\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R\to\mathfrak u(V_i)$ is the derived Lie-algebra representation. Set $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$ and $f=dB$, and write $A_i:=\rho_{i*}(A,iB)$ and $F_i:=dA_i+A_i\wedge A_i$; thus $D_{\mu,i}=\partial_\mu+(A_i)_\mu$. For $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$, $A_E=A+iB I_3$ and $F_E=F_A+ifI_3$; for $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$, $A_{E^*}=-A^T-iB I_3$ and $F_{E^*}=-F_A^T-ifI_3$. Local transformations are $A\mapsto g^{-1}Ag+g^{-1}dg$ and $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ for compactly supported $g: M\to SU(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$; the $U(1)$ group element is $e^{i\alpha}$. Let $c$ be the ghost-number-one odd $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ ghost and $\eta$ the ghost-number-one odd real $U(1)_V$ ghost. The finite-jet BRST differential for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{su}(3)\oplus i\mathbb R$ is specified on components by $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-[c,c]/2$, $sB_\mu=\partial_\mu\eta$, $s\eta=0$, and $s\psi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c,i\eta)\psi_i$; it acts on jets by commuting with total derivatives. The $U(1)_V$ factor is central. On horizontal forms use the supplier's extension $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$, so $sd_H+d_Hs=0$. In particular the whole one-form obeys $sB=-d_H\eta$; the positive component rule is not a whole-form equation.

For an ordinary compactly supported infinitesimal parameter $\epsilon=\epsilon^aT_a:M\to\mathfrak{su}(3)$ and $\alpha:M\to\mathbb R$, define a linear map $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ from ghost-number-one background horizontal $p$-forms to ordinary $p$-forms. In the unique normal form with all $dx$ factors to the left and the single ghost jet to the right, replace $c_I^a$ by $\partial_I\epsilon^a$ and $\eta_I$ by $\partial_I\alpha$, leaving background jets unchanged. Every such form has precisely one ghost factor because the background algebra has no negative-ghost generators. This is a linear map on that homogeneous component, not an algebra homomorphism on the exterior ghost algebra. It commutes with $d_H$. If $C_p$ is ghost-free, the finite-jet chain rule gives $\mathcal E^p_{\epsilon,\alpha}(sC_p)=(-1)^p\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}C_p$: the sign moves $s$ past the $p$ coordinate one-forms, and the component rules give the ordinary infinitesimal field variation. Thus in physical degree four $\mathcal E^4(sC_4)=\delta C_4$, and $d_H$-exact terms evaluate to ordinary total derivatives. The degree-five descent is first formed on the formal auxiliary extension used for the degree-six polynomial, before restriction to $M$; there $\mathcal E^5(sI_5)=-\delta I_5$. Consequently $sI_5+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$ yields the physical convention $\delta I_5=d_H\mathcal E^4(I_4^{(1)})$.

The anomaly-matching data include one common Pauli–Villars subtraction prescription for the chiral triangle graphs, with opposite-statistics regulator fields and regulator masses taken to the large-mass limit, together with the consistent effective-action variation convention and compact-support boundary conditions. The local anomaly complex is the finite-jet background subalgebra generated by $A,B$ and their BRST ghosts, with no matter-field jets, so its ghost-number-zero four-forms are precisely the admitted local counterterms. We quotient by all such finite-jet local counterterms and by compactly supported total derivatives; no background-gauge-invariance condition is imposed on an individual counterterm. In particular, for real dimensionless $\lambda$, the four-form $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ is admitted, where $K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}(A\wedge dA+\tfrac23A\wedge A\wedge A)$. As an explicit source-backed one-loop input, after the regulator masses are taken to infinity this selected prescription assigns to each positive-chirality species $R_i$ the consistent local anomaly obtained by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$ of the preceding cubic-polynomial definition. The fixed linear descent map is normalized by $\mathcal I_6=dI^{(0)}_5$, $sI^{(0)}_5+d_HI^{(1)}_4=0$, and $sI^{(1)}_4+d_HI^{(2)}_3=0$, with $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_{i\in S}\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I^{(1)}_4(R_i,A_i))$. This determinant law is an adopted regulator input in the data, not a locally derived theorem about every regulator. The total polynomial is $\mathcal I_6^{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{i\in S}\mathcal I_6(R_i,A_i)$, and its local anomaly class is interpreted using the preceding local ’t Hooft-anomaly definition. No large-transformation test, torsion calculation, mixed gravitational term, dynamical gauge quantization, or continuum-existence result is included.

current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current batch-41 local-anomaly Definition inspected and used only to distinguish its infinitesimal class from determinant-line holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 4 from the current supplier graph.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix an even integer $d\ge2$, a compact smooth oriented Riemannian $d$-manifold $M$ without boundary with a specified spin structure, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$ with connection $A$, and a unitary finite-dimensional complex representation $R:G\to U(V_R)$. Let $E_R=P\times_R V_R$ be the associated Hermitian bundle. Let $S^+$ and $S^-$ be the associated bundles of the two half-spin representations of $\operatorname{Spin}(d)$. The chiral Dirac operator is the first-order operator

$$D^+_{A,R}:H^1(M;S^+\otimes E_R)\longrightarrow L^2(M;S^-\otimes E_R),$$

where $H^1$ and $L^2$ are the first Sobolev and square-integrable completions for the fixed Riemannian metric. Assume the operator is Fredholm. Its inverse determinant line is

$$\mathcal L_A=\left(\det_{\mathbb C}\ker D^+_{A,R}\right)^*\otimes\det_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{coker}D^+_{A,R},$$

Here $\det_{\mathbb C}W=\bigwedge^{\dim_{\mathbb C}W}_{\mathbb C}W$, including $\det0=\mathbb C$. Our phrase **inverse determinant line** means the dual of $\Delta_A=\det\ker D^+\otimes(\det\operatorname{coker}D^+)^*$; the displayed $\mathcal L$ is the line called $\mathrm{Det}$, not $\mathrm{Det}^{-1}$, in Dai–Freed §2. This explicit formula fixes the convention throughout.

The named regularized geometry means the following supplied **admissible analytic data**, rather than an arbitrary Hermitian line relabeled by a name. Test smooth dependence on each finite-dimensional smooth parameter manifold $T$ of connections on the fixed $M,P,R$. Write $\mathscr H^\pm=T\times L^2(M;S^\pm\otimes E_R)$ with common first-Sobolev domains. Supply unitary parameter connections $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ on these Hilbert bundles, preserving smooth sections and the Sobolev domains; for the fixed product identification one may take the ordinary derivative in $T$. Fix a positive inverse-length scale $\mu$ and put $\mathscr D=D^+/\mu$, with Hilbert adjoint $\mathscr D^*$. These choices and the local-counterterm convention are fixed before phases are compared.

Require $Q^+=\mathscr D^*\mathscr D$ and $Q^-=\mathscr D\mathscr D^*$ to have the supplied nonnegative self-adjoint realizations with discrete spectrum, finite multiplicities and smooth eigensections, and the same positive spectrum with multiplicity. A spectral cut is a number $a>0$ not in either spectrum on an open parameter patch $U_a\subseteq T$. The orthogonal projections onto eigenvalues $\lambda<a$, including zero modes, must form smooth finite-rank bundles $V_a^\pm\subset\mathscr H^\pm$; their complements are denoted $\mathscr H^\pm_{>a}$. The finite cut line is $L_a=(\det V_a^+)^*\otimes\det V_a^-$. For $a<b$, the operator $\mathscr D$ is invertible between the eigenbundles $V_{(a,b)}^+$ and $V_{(a,b)}^-$. Glue $L_a$ to $L_b$ by tensoring with its top exterior power $\det\mathscr D_{(a,b)}$. Finite-dimensional cancellation of these invertible modes identifies each fiber with the displayed kernel/cokernel line, even where kernel dimensions jump. Tensor factors are kept in increasing cut order; parity is $\operatorname{ind}D^+\bmod2$ if graded lines are used.

For each cut, define the scalar function $\zeta_a(z)=\sum_{\lambda>a}\lambda^{-z}$ using the positive $Q^+$ eigenvalues with multiplicity and real $\log\lambda$. Admissibility requires convergence on an initial right half-plane, a specified meromorphic continuation to a connected domain reaching $z=0$, regularity there, and smooth parameter dependence of $\zeta'_a(0)$. The **Quillen squared norm** is $\|\ell\|_Q^2=\exp(-\zeta'_a(0))\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$. Finite bands satisfy $\zeta_a-\zeta_b=\sum_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda^{-z}$ and $\|\ell_b\|_{L^2}^2=(\prod_{a<\lambda<b}\lambda)\|\ell_a\|_{L^2}^2$, which give cut independence of this norm. No existence of that continuation for an arbitrary Fredholm family is inferred.

Project $\widetilde\nabla^\pm$ to the cut subbundles and their complements. They induce a connection $\nabla^a$ on $L_a$. On the invertible complement let $\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a}=\widetilde\nabla^-_{>a}\mathscr D_{>a}-\mathscr D_{>a}\widetilde\nabla^+_{>a}$. For $t>0$ define the complex one-form $h_a(t)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathscr H^+_{>a}}(\mathscr D_{>a}^{-1}(\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D_{>a})e^{-tQ^+_{>a}})$; the trace is the absolutely convergent sum of diagonal matrix coefficients in an orthonormal eigenbasis, independent of choices within each eigenspace. Require this convergence and the smooth coefficient expansion $h_a(t)=\sum_{j=-d/2}^{-1}b_jt^j+b_0+b_{\log}\log t+o(1)$ as dimensionless $t\downarrow0$. The finite-part convention is $\operatorname{FP}h_a=b_0+\gamma_1b_{\log}$, where $\gamma_1=\int_0^\infty e^{-r}\log r\,dr=\Gamma'(1)$; the equality names the usual gamma-function derivative and fixes the log-term subtraction. The **Bismut–Freed connection** in this convention is the local formula $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}=\nabla^a+\operatorname{FP}h_a$, as in Dai–Freed (3.6)–(3.7).

Admissibility further requires that these forms are smooth, intertwine the specified cut transitions, and are compatible with the Quillen norm: $d\|s\|_Q^2=\langle\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s,s\rangle_Q+\langle s,\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}s\rangle_Q$ for every local section $s$. Thus in a unit frame the connection form is purely imaginary. Gauge identifications must intertwine all cut data, preserve this norm and preserve the connection after the corresponding parameter pullback. These are explicit mathematical conditions on the supplied regularization. Cut gluing reduces on a finite band to the determinant derivative $(\det\mathscr D)^{-1}\nabla(\det\mathscr D)=\operatorname{Tr}(\mathscr D^{-1}\widetilde\nabla\mathscr D)$ with the induced finite-dimensional connections; analytic existence, smooth heat expansions and naturality for all geometric families are not asserted here. In particular a Hermitian line alone does not supply this connection. Parallel transport means the solution of $\nabla^{\mathrm{BF}}_{\dot A_t}s(t)=0$ with a specified initial value; in a unit frame with connection $i\beta$, it is multiplication by $\exp(-i\int\beta)$.

When the supplied real or pseudoreal fermion structure instead yields a skew-Fredholm quadratic form, include its actual **Pfaffian data**. Concretely, on a common dense Sobolev domain $W^1$ of a complex Hilbert space $W^0$, supply a bounded linear Fredholm map $B:W^1\to(W^0)^*$ such that $b(w,z)=(Bw)(z)$ is complex bilinear and skew on $W^1\times W^1$, with $\operatorname{coker}B\cong(\ker B)^*$ induced by the pairing. Supply finite spectral subspaces $W_a$ of $B^*B$ containing the kernel, with orthogonal cut bands on which $b$ is nondegenerate and no cross terms between bands. For a finite $2m$-dimensional space $W$ the Pfaffian is $\operatorname{pf}(b)=b^{\wedge m}/m!\in\det W^*$, interpreting $b\in\bigwedge^2W^*$; it is zero in odd dimension. Glue $P_a=\det W_a^*$ by the nonzero Pfaffians of the even-dimensional invertible cut bands. The resulting graded line $P$ has parity $\dim\ker B\bmod2$ and the specified natural square identification $P^{\otimes2}\cong L_B$, where $L_B$ is the displayed determinant convention applied to $B$. Its squared Quillen norm has high-mode factor $\exp(-\zeta'_{B,a}(0)/2)$, with $\zeta_{B,a}$ defined from $B^*B$ exactly as above. Its unitary connection is the one whose tensor square, under that identification, is the supplied Bismut–Freed connection of $L_B$; locally its connection form is half that determinant form in square-compatible frames. Smooth gluing, the square identification, spectral continuations, metric compatibility and gauge naturality are required Pfaffian admissibility data, not an arbitrary choice of a square root or an existence assertion for every real/pseudoreal theory.

Let $\mathcal A(P)$ be the affine space of smooth connections on $P$, and let $\mathcal G(P)$ be the group of smooth bundle automorphisms covering the identity on $M$. A gauge arrow $u:A\to A^u$ induces a unitary map $u_*:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_{A^u}$ by its action on kernel and cokernel. A closed loop in background/gauge-field space consists of a smooth path $A_t$ in $\mathcal A(P)$, $0\le t\le1$, and an endpoint gauge arrow $u:A_0\to A_1$. current_declaration.statement:
Assume AC. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$, $W=\mathbb C^N$, $N\ge1$, $k\ge0$, and let $x=(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ satisfy the raw complex equation $\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. Put $K=V\oplus V\oplus W$. For $z=(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2$ put

$$a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T,\qquad b_z=(-B_2^\dagger+\bar z_2,B_1^\dagger-\bar z_1,I^\dagger)^T,\qquad D_z=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger\\a_z^\dagger\end{pmatrix}.$$

Then

$$D_zD_z^\dagger=\begin{pmatrix}b_z^\dagger b_z&\mu_{\mathbb C}\\\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger&a_z^\dagger a_z\end{pmatrix},\qquad b_z^\dagger b_z-a_z^\dagger a_z=\mu_{\mathbb R}.$$

The maps $b_z^\dagger$ are onto for every $z$ exactly when the datum is stable; the maps $a_z$ are injective for every $z$ exactly when it is costable. Consequently, when both moments vanish, regularity is equivalent to $D_z$ being onto for every $z$. On this locus $f_z=a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z$ is positive definite and

$$P_z=1-D_z^\dagger\operatorname{diag}(f_z^{-1},f_z^{-1})D_z$$

is the smooth orthogonal projection onto a rank-$N$ bundle over $\mathbb R^4$. The projection connection $\nabla=P\,d$ is unitary and satisfies $F^+=0$ for the positive stereographic orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, where $z_1=x^0+ix^1$, $z_2=x^2+ix^3$.

In homogeneous coordinates $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2]$ on $\mathbb P^3$, put $A=B_1\lambda_1-B_2^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_1$, $C=B_2\lambda_1+B_1^\dagger\lambda_2-\mu_2$ and

$$\alpha=(A,C,J\lambda_1+I^\dagger\lambda_2)^T,\qquad\beta=(-C,A,I\lambda_1-J^\dagger\lambda_2).$$

The polynomial identity is $\beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C}+\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R}-\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger$. With $\sigma(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$, one has $\beta(v)=\alpha(\sigma v)^\dagger$. The real line over $z$ is $\mu_1=z_1\lambda_1-\bar z_2\lambda_2$, $\mu_2=z_2\lambda_1+\bar z_1\lambda_2$; the line at infinity is $\lambda_1=\lambda_2=0$. For regular zero-moment data these maps form a holomorphic bundle monad, trivial on each real line, with middle cohomology on the line over $z$ canonically $\ker D_z$. Its framing at infinity is $W$. The torus acts on the homogeneous coordinates by $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ and on the raw data by $(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$; the monad isomorphism has source, middle and target factors $(t_1t_2)^{-1}$, $\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)$ and $1$, respectively. It preserves the framing representation $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$.

This proves a forward raw block construction. It does not assert that every real Ward monad has this normal form, that its inverse extraction is unique, or that the connection extends with charge $k$; those global correspondence and charge assertions require their separate proofs.

current_declaration.title: Determinant flatness and charge normalization for framed U(N) ASD data
current_declaration.statement:
Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $E\to S^4$ be a smooth Hermitian rank-$N$ vector bundle with $N\geq2$, a smooth unitary connection $A$, and a unitary framing at $\infty$. Give $S^4$ the round metric and the orientation specified in the definition of the framed ASD sector, and assume $F_A^+=0$. Then the induced determinant-line connection on $\det E=\Lambda^N E$ is flat. Its framing at $\infty$ determines a unique global unit parallel section, so the framed unitary bundle reduces to a framed $SU(N)$ bundle. With $q_N=-(8\pi^2)^{-1}\int_{S^4}\operatorname{tr}_N(F_A\wedge F_A)$ and the determinant Chern-form convention $c(A)=\det(I-F_A/(2\pi i))$, one has

$$q_N(E,A)=-\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle\in-\mathbb Z_{\geq0}.$$

Thus $k=-q_N=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle$ is a nonnegative integer, with the sign corresponding to the anti-self-dual equation $F_A^+=0$.

current_declaration.title: Coherent-section quotient topologies are Fréchet and presentation-independent
current_declaration.statement: Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional complex manifold, let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_M$-module, and let $V$ be a nonempty open subset of one holomorphic chart on which a finite presentation $\mathcal O_V^{p_1}\to\mathcal O_V^{p_0}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal F|_V\to0$ is fixed. Assume that the induced section map $\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V^{p_0})\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal F)$ is surjective. Then its quotient topology from compact-convergence on $\mathcal O(V)^{p_0}$ is a Fréchet topology. If two such presentations are locally defined on a common cover and both section maps are surjective, their quotient topologies agree; the compatible-family topology on sections over any open set admitting a countable cover by such presentation neighborhoods is also Fréchet and independent of the chosen chart cover and presentations.

current_declaration.title: Unique chain lifting and sigma-Hermitian monad duality
current_declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited through the analytic scalar-cohomology input; the finite matrix duality is choice-free.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ carry the antiholomorphic coordinate involution $\sigma([\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2])=[-\bar\lambda_2:\bar\lambda_1:-\bar\mu_2:\bar\mu_1]$. A linear monad is a locally split exact complex at its ends
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
with locally free middle cohomology $F=\ker\beta/\operatorname{im}\alpha$, where $U,S,U'$ are finite-dimensional complex vector spaces. For a degree-one matrix $P(z)$ put $P^\#(z)=P(jz)^\dagger$ and define the signed dual monad $D(M):(U')^*\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\xrightarrow{-\beta^\#}S^*\otimes\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\alpha^\#}U^*\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; its cohomology is denoted $D(F)$, and dualizing twice uses $(P^\#)^\#=-P$ and $D^2(M)=M$. By a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing we mean an isomorphism $h_F:F\to D(F)$ that is linear in its first variable, conjugate-linear in its second, and fixed by this bidual operation. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$. For any two such monads, every holomorphic morphism of their middle cohomology bundles lifts to a unique constant chain map between the monads. In particular, for a monad with a nondegenerate holomorphic $\sigma$-Hermitian self-pairing, the unique lift is a chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle map $H=H^\dagger$ and normalized identities
$$
\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H,\qquad \beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z),
$$
where $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$ and the end spaces are identified by the lifted pairing.

current_declaration.physical_scope: A local formal Lorenz-gauge functional in the finite-jet Yang–Mills BRST algebra; no global slice, continuum measure, or empirical prediction is asserted.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ be a nonempty open region with compact support or boundary conditions that remove total-derivative terms. Work in the adopted pure $SU(2)$ model, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ and normalized positive $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, extended bilinearly to the graded coefficient algebra. In the finite-jet algebra take $A_\mu$ to be an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $1$, $c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$, $\bar c$ an odd $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ an even $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued field of ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$. Let $\xi>0$ be dimensionless. Use the Lie-algebra bracket and odd left BRST derivation

$$sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],\qquad sc=-\tfrac12[c,c],\qquad s\bar c=b,\qquad sb=0,$$

extended to jets by commuting with total derivatives. Define the Lorenz-gauge fermion and its BRST-exact functional by

$$\Psi_\xi=\int_U d^4x\,\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu A_\mu+\tfrac{\xi}{2}b),\qquad S_{\rm gf}:=s\Psi_\xi.$$

Then

$$S_{\rm gf}=\int_U d^4x\,\left(\kappa(b,\partial^\mu A_\mu)+\tfrac{\xi}{2}\kappa(b,b)-\kappa(\bar c,\partial^\mu D_\mu c)\right),\qquad D_\mu c:=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c],$$

is a local, even, ghost-number-zero functional of density dimension $4$, and it is BRST-closed. It is an exact gauge-fixing term in the formal local algebra; this example does not claim a global representative for every gauge orbit or a continuum functional measure.

current_declaration.physical_scope: Formal coefficientwise Slavnov–Taylor identities for the adopted pure SU(2) Yang–Mills perturbation theory, conditional on the QAP and local anomaly exactness; no continuum measure, convergence, nonperturbative existence, or empirical prediction is asserted.
current_declaration.statement:
In the axiom base inherited from the adopted model, fix the classical pure $SU(2)$ Yang–Mills model on oriented, time-oriented Minkowski spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, its selected smooth right-principal bundle sector $P\to M$, no matter fields, invariant form $\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and fixed $g_{\rm YM}>0$. Let $U\subset M$ be a nonempty local trivialization chart, use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, and use the right-action curvature convention $F_A=dA+\tfrac12[A\wedge A]$. The adopted local classical action density is $-\kappa(F_A\wedge *_\eta F_A)/(2g_{\rm YM}^2)$. The local gauge potential $A_\mu$ is even with ghost number $0$ and engineering dimension $1$; the odd ghost $c$ has ghost number $1$ and dimension $0$. Define $D_\mu c=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$ and the minimal BRST transformations $sA_\mu=D_\mu c$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$. When the nonminimal pair is included, let $\bar c$ be odd with ghost number $-1$ and dimension $2$, and $b$ even with ghost number $0$ and dimension $2$, with $s\bar c=b$ and $sb=0$. Antifields have the opposite field parity and ghost number $-1-\operatorname{gh}(\Phi)$, with engineering dimensions chosen so $\Phi^*s\Phi$ has density dimension $4$.

Use the canonical BV antibracket and let the classical BV functional be the pure-gauge extension
$$\Gamma_0=S_0+\int_U d^4x\left(A^{*\mu}_a(D_\mu c)^a+\tfrac12c^*_a[c,c]^a-\bar c^*_ab\right),$$
where the nonminimal term is omitted if that pair is not included, and $S_0$ denotes the adopted classical action on the chosen domain. Assume $\Gamma_0$ is even, has ghost number zero, satisfies $\tfrac12(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_0)=0$, and the chosen local BV functional domain has no nonzero central element of ghost number one. The model postulate and its classical gauge-invariance theorem are explicit inputs fixing and interpreting $S_0$; neither is proved by this theorem.

Choose the local Lorenz gauge $\partial^\mu A_\mu=0$ with constant $\xi>0$, dimensional regularization $D=4-2\epsilon$, modified minimal subtraction of $1/\epsilon$ poles together with $-\gamma_E+\log(4\pi)$, and a finite engineering-dimension bound $d_*$. The allowed counterterms are integrated Lorentz-scalar finite-jet polynomials of ghost number zero and dimension at most $d_*$ in $A,c,\bar c,b$, their antifields, and their spacetime derivatives. The formal loop variable $\lambda$ is dimensionless; $\Gamma(\lambda)=\Gamma_0+\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\Gamma_n$ is a formal coefficient sequence with no convergence at nonzero $\lambda$ asserted. Write $\Gamma^{(<n)}$ for a partial action whose coefficients below order $n$ already satisfy the Slavnov identity.

Assume the local quantum action principle (QAP): at each first failing order $n$ there are a local ghost-number-one four-form $\delta_n$ of engineering dimension at most $d_*$ and local ghost-number-two three-form $\rho_n$ of dimension at most $d_*-1$ such that
$$\mathfrak S(\Gamma^{(<n)})=\lambda^n\int_U\delta_n+O(\lambda^{n+1}),\qquad B_{\Gamma_0}\delta_n+d_H\rho_n=0,$$
where $\mathfrak S(\Gamma)=\tfrac12(\Gamma,\Gamma)$, $B_{\Gamma_0}X=(\Gamma_0,X)$, and $d_H=dx^\mu D_\mu$ is the horizontal differential on finite-jet local forms. Assume local anomaly cancellation in the explicit form of a supplied sequence of allowed ghost-number-zero four-forms $\Xi_n$ and ghost-number-one three-forms $\Theta_n$ satisfying
$$\delta_n=B_{\Gamma_0}\Xi_n+d_H\Theta_n$$
at every first failing order; put $\Xi_n=\Theta_n=0$ at nonfailing orders. Compact support or the model's boundary conditions make the integral of each $d_H$-exact four-form vanish. Then the counterterm series $C(\lambda)=-\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda^n\int_U\Xi_n$ yields $\mathfrak S(\Gamma(\lambda)+C(\lambda))=0$ coefficientwise.

For $g\in\{0,1\}$, restrict $H^{g,4}(s\mid d_H)$, with $s=B_{\Gamma_0}$, to local cocycles of engineering dimension at most $d_*$; identify two allowed representatives when their difference is $sm+d_Hn$ for local forms of the indicated ghost numbers and the difference remains in the allowed power-counting space. The resulting ghost-number-zero quotient is exactly the local counterterm freedom modulo trivial counterterms and total derivatives. The ghost-number-one quotient classifies local obstruction classes in that space; a nonzero class cannot be removed by an allowed local counterterm. This is a quotient statement and asserts no finite basis of representatives. The conclusion is conditional on the local QAP and supplied anomaly-cancellation sequence; it proves neither premise and asserts no empirical result, continuum functional measure, convergence, or nonperturbative existence. Any finite-dimensional Faddeev–Popov Jacobian remains the ordinary Jacobian of its specified regulated group action and transverse slice; it is not a continuum functional determinant.

current_declaration.title: Local N=1 Wilsonian Superspace Action Data
current_declaration.statement:
Use the physical action brackets $[U]_D=-I_D(U)/4$ and $[Y]_F=I_F(Y)/2$ from [[def-qftx-physical-superspace-normalization]], with raw mathematical coefficient integrals $I_D,I_F$ unchanged. Physical chiral components obey $\psi_{\mathrm{raw}}=\sqrt2\psi$ and $F_{\mathrm{raw}}=2F$. All physical action and coupling formulas below use these brackets and physical component names; adding Hermitian conjugation applies only to the F action and occurs once.

Use the flat four-dimensional N=1 superspace conventions in natural units $c=\hbar=1$, with $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$, metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, and the ordered Grassmann generators, Berezin measures, chiral constraint, and covariant derivatives fixed by the earlier superspace definitions. Fix the global gauge group as a compact closed matrix subgroup $G\subset U(N)$; this chosen subgroup, rather than only its Lie algebra, is part of the data. Let $\mathfrak g$ be its finite-dimensional real Lie algebra, let $\mathcal H_i$ be finite-dimensional Hermitian spaces, and let $\rho_i:G\to U(\mathcal H_i)$ be smooth unitary representations for a finite family of chiral superfields $\Phi_i$. Work on the trivial bundle $M\times G$ and expand in the topologically trivial sector. Let $A_\mu$ be the connection component of the vector prepotential in a local trivialization. For the odd ghost $c$, use the non-Abelian BRST transformations $sA_\mu=\partial_\mu c+[A_\mu,c]$, $sc=-\tfrac12[c,c]$, and $s\Phi_i=-\rho_{i*}(c)\Phi_i$ on component fields and jets.

A vector prepotential $V$ is a dimensionless even Hermitian matrix-valued superfield in the chosen faithful representation of $G$. Representation maps below mean the complex-linear extension of the Lie-algebra differential, rather than evaluation of a group representation on a Lie-algebra element. Write $V_i$ for this represented prepotential. Let $\Lambda$ be an even chiral complexified Lie-algebra parameter, write $h_i=e^{-\Lambda_i}$, and define the Hermitian matter kernel $\mathscr H_i=e^{-V_i}$. The supergauge laws are $\Phi_i\mapsto h_i\Phi_i$ and $\mathscr H_i\mapsto(h_i^\dagger)^{-1}\mathscr H_i h_i^{-1}$. Define the curvature using this SAME matter kernel:

$$W_\alpha=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(\mathscr H^{-1}D_\alpha\mathscr H)=-\tfrac14\bar D^{\dot\beta}\bar D_{\dot\beta}(e^{V}D_\alpha e^{-V}).$$

It is chiral and transforms by $W_\alpha\mapsto hW_\alpha h^{-1}$. Indeed, with $D_\alpha(h^\dagger)^{-1}=0$, the transformed logarithmic derivative is $h\mathscr H^{-1}(D_\alpha\mathscr H)h^{-1}+hD_\alpha h^{-1}$. The chiral projection of the second term vanishes: $\bar D_{\dot\beta}h=0$ and the superspace derivative anticommutator makes $\bar D^2D_\alpha h^{-1}=0$. Chiral projection of the first term gives the stated conjugation law. The matter density is invariant because $\Phi_i'^\dagger\mathscr H_i'\Phi_i'=\Phi_i^\dagger\mathscr H_i\Phi_i$.

For each simple factor choose a fixed invariant quadratic trace functional $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}$ (including its normalization and sign), and set $\tau=\vartheta/(2\pi)+4\pi i/g_{\mathrm h}^2$. The gauge density uses $\tau\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)/(8\pi i)$; the quadratic functional and $g_{\mathrm h}$ together, not a symbol $g$ alone, determine its normalization. Product groups have one such choice per factor. For a fixed normalized trace, $g_{\mathrm h}$ occurs in $\tau$, not in the prepotential exponential.

The exact classical bridge to [[def-qftx-n1-vector-superfield]] is at fixed real $g=g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$: set $V=-2gV_{30}$, $\Lambda=-i\Lambda_{30}$ and $\mathscr H=e^{2gV_{30}}$. Then $h=e^{i\Lambda_{30}}$, the matter kernel and its gauge law agree, and $W_\alpha=\mathscr C_{\alpha,30}$ is the earlier REPRESENTED matrix curvature by substitution. The earlier abstract Lie-algebra-valued curvature instead satisfies $\rho_*(\mathcal W_{\alpha,30})=W_\alpha/(2i)$, because $W_\alpha=2g t_aW^a_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}$ and $\mathcal W_{\alpha,30}=gT_aW^a_{\mathrm{can},\alpha}$ with $t_a=iT_a$. The connection remains $A_\mu=-igB_\mu$, with the same component BRST law. For this selected $SU(2)$ bridge use the ordinary defining trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}=\operatorname{Tr}_2$. Then

$$\frac{1}{4g^2}\kappa_{\mathbb C}(\mathcal W^\alpha_{30},\mathcal W_{\alpha,30})=\frac{1}{8g^2}\operatorname{Tr}_2(W^\alpha W_\alpha).$$

The holomorphic datum writes this coefficient as $\tau\operatorname{Tr}_2(W^\alpha W_\alpha)/(8\pi i)$. Therefore at zero topological angle the exact parameter match is $\tau=\pi i/g^2$, or $g_{\mathrm h}=2g$ in the displayed definition $\tau=4\pi i/g_{\mathrm h}^2$. This factor is derived from the matrix-versus-Lie curvature dictionary, not removed by changing the trace sign. Hermitian conjugation is added once on both sides of the chiral equality; the real D-term is not doubled. The selected earlier models have zero theta term, so no global theta-period or D'Hoker prepotential conversion is asserted here. These are identities of classical densities at fixed real parameters, with no quantum change of variables, anomalous Jacobian, holomorphic canonical normalization or equality of regulated measures.

A local rigid N=1 action datum has the fixed canonical matter kinetic term $\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i$, an additional real gauge-invariant formal power series $G(\Phi,\bar\Phi,V,\partial_\mu,D_\alpha,\bar D_{\dot\alpha})$, and a holomorphic gauge-invariant formal power series $F(\Phi,W)$. The additional $G$ may contain local spacetime or superspace derivatives; $F$ contains no such derivatives, anti-chiral variables, or spacetime dependence. Its formal ultraviolet-cutoff density is

$$\mathcal L_{\Lambda_0}=[\sum_i\Phi_i^\dagger e^{-V_i}\Phi_i+G]_D+2\operatorname{Re}[\frac{\tau}{8\pi i}\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathrm h}(W^\alpha W_\alpha)+F(\Phi,W)]_F.$$

In a two-derivative scalar sector, a real function $K(\phi,\bar\phi)$ of the scalar components $\phi_i$ is a Kähler potential, and its Hermitian matrix $g_{i\bar j}=\partial^2 K/(\partial\phi_i\partial\bar\phi_j)$ is the associated Kähler metric wherever it is nondegenerate. These are particular data in the real D-term, not part of the holomorphic F-term.

Here $[\Phi_i]=1$, $[W_\alpha]=3/2$, $[g]=0$, $[\tau]=0$, the F-term integrand has mass dimension three, and the D-term integrand has mass dimension two; dimensionful coefficients in nonrenormalizable interactions carry the dimensions needed to make the density have mass dimension four. A Wilsonian prescription with cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$ formally separates Euclidean momentum modes with $|q|\geq\lambda$ from modes with $|p|<\lambda$. Let $S_\lambda^{\mathrm{vert}}$ denote the coefficientwise functional assigned by the selected cutoff prescription. For this definition, its perturbative vertex coefficients are assumed to be sums of one-particle-irreducible graphs in that prescribed expansion: cutting a single internal propagator line cannot disconnect a graph counted as one vertex. This is an explicit property of the selected formal vertex functional, not a theorem about generic partial integration in an interacting theory. Assume also that $S_\lambda^{\mathrm{vert}}$ has a local derivative expansion in local terms with finitely many derivatives at each formal perturbative order for external momenta $|p|\ll\lambda$. Write its density using $G_\lambda$, $F_\lambda$, and $\tau_\lambda$ in the same form as $\mathcal L_{\Lambda_0}$.

A regulated formal expectation $\langle\mathcal O\rangle_\lambda$ is the normalized coefficientwise functional assigned by a specified cutoff prescription; the notation asserts no convergence or physical continuum measure. A local insertion $\mathcal O$ is a polynomial or formal local function of the fields and finitely many spacetime derivatives, multiplied by a compactly supported test function. For an insertion $\mathcal O$ and the rigid supersymmetry variation generated by the N=1 supercharges, its Ward identity is the change-of-variables equation $\langle\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}\mathcal O\rangle_\lambda=\langle\mathcal O\,\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}S_\lambda\rangle_\lambda$. The BRST Ward identity is $\langle s\mathcal O\rangle_\lambda=0$ when $sS_\lambda=0$. A local gauge anomaly is a nonzero local insertion in the latter identity. A regulator preserves these Ward identities when the equations hold coefficientwise at every perturbative order without an anomaly insertion; this definition does not assert that such a regulator exists for every field representation.

The spurion argument additionally uses the local background extension of this formal prescription: independent F coefficients and $\tau$ are nondynamical chiral superfields, and independent real D coefficients are unconstrained real superfields. The prescribed regulated counterterms obey the same superspace and gauge Ward identities for these backgrounds and have a local derivative expansion in them. The derivative-free chiral sector is evaluated at constant scalar backgrounds after that extension; background-superderivative terms belong to the real D sector after chiral projection. This is the usual spurion-compatible regulator hypothesis, not a consequence of classical BRST nilpotence or a regulator-existence theorem. Its counterterms depend on the original background coefficients, so a redundant parametrization of those coefficients introduces no independent physical coupling. No rescaling of an integrated matter or vector field is assumed in this extension.

The component background fields are smooth on $M$, and admissible variations and insertions are compactly supported or satisfy decay conditions that make the stated total-derivative boundary terms vanish. Loop momenta are regulated separately by the Wilsonian high-mode prescription.

For a U(1) factor, normalize its gauge parameter as $e^{i\alpha}$ with period $2\pi$. Each chiral matter representation decomposes into integer charge weights $q_{i,a}$; the total charge trace $\sum_i\sum_a q_{i,a}$ counts each weight with its multiplicity. In the stated supergauge convention the real Abelian vector prepotential $V_1$ shifts by the negative of a chiral parameter and its conjugate. Under compact-support or vanishing-boundary-term conditions, the physical action $\int d^4x\,[\xi V_1]_D$ is gauge invariant for constant $\xi$ and is called a Fayet–Iliopoulos term; $\xi$ is its field-independent coefficient. For an Abelian fixed-$g$ component bridge, $V_1=-2gV_{30}$ gives $[\xi V_1]_D=-g\xi D_B$ in the auxiliary sector. Thus the coefficient $\xi_D$ of $+D_B$ is $\xi_D=-g\xi$ in this convention; no differently signed source FI symbol is silently identified. This definition specifies formal action and cutoff data only; it does not assert that a gauge-invariant supersymmetric regulator exists for every field representation or that the perturbative series converges.

current_declaration.title: A mixed-background counterterm shifts the local representative
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $A$ be a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ connection one-form on trivial $\mathbb R^{1,3}$, with curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$, and let $B$ be a smooth real $U(1)_V$ background one-form with compactly supported gauge parameter $\alpha$. In natural units, $[A]=[B]=\text{mass}$ and $[F_A]=\text{mass}^2$. Define the local three-form

$$K_3(A):=\operatorname{tr}\left(A\wedge dA+\frac23A\wedge A\wedge A\right)$$

and add the four-dimensional local counterterm $C_4=\lambda B\wedge K_3(A)$ to the effective action, with dimensionless coefficient $\lambda$. Under the $U(1)_V$ background transformation $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$ with $A$ fixed, its local variation is

$$\delta_\alpha C_4=\lambda\,d(\alpha K_3(A))-\lambda\,\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A).$$

The first term integrates to a boundary term and vanishes for compactly supported $\alpha$. Thus this counterterm shifts the $U(1)_V$ component of the local anomaly representative by $-\lambda\alpha\operatorname{tr}(F_A\wedge F_A)$ while the full relative class is unchanged modulo the admitted counterterm space. This calculation does not assert that the full $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ anomaly vanishes or that the $SU(3)$ component of the representative is unchanged.

current_declaration.statement:
Use the same flat-space background convention but take the spectrum to contain only one positive-chirality species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$. Its polynomial is

$$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right),$$

where $F_A$ is the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature, $f=dB$ is the $U(1)_V$ curvature, and the expression is evaluated as a degree-six polynomial on the formal extension used for descent. The mixed $U(1)_V$–$SU(3)^2$ term and the pure $U(1)_V^3$ term have nonzero coefficients. This example verifies that the one-field polynomial is not the zero invariant polynomial; it does not claim that the associated relative BRST class is nontrivial modulo every admissible counterterm or that a global anomaly has been evaluated.

current_declaration.title: Local anomaly cancellation for a conjugate chiral pair
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current interface, source evidence, and readiness are recorded in batch-41 notes.
current_declaration.statement:
Use the selected flat-space anomaly-matching model on oriented $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-,+,+,+)$ and natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Its nondynamical global-symmetry backgrounds are a smooth compactly supported anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ connection $A$ and a smooth compactly supported real $U(1)_V$ connection $B$ on the trivial bundles. The finite field spectrum consists of two massless positive-chirality Weyl species, one in $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and one in its dual $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. The background is not integrated over. Use one common large-mass Pauli–Villars subtraction scheme and the consistent effective-action convention fixed in the model data.

Adopt the source-backed one-loop input that each positive-chirality species in this regulator has consistent local variation given by descent from $\mathcal I_6(R)=2\pi[\operatorname{tr}_R\exp(-iF_R/(2\pi))]_6$, with the same linear descent for every species: $\mathcal I_6=dI_5^{(0)}$, $sI_5^{(0)}+d_HI_4^{(1)}=0$, and $sI_4^{(1)}+d_HI_3^{(2)}=0$, and $\delta_{\epsilon,\alpha}\Gamma=\sum_R\int_M\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}(I_4^{(1)}(R))$. Here $s$ is the component BRST differential extended with $s(dx^\mu\wedge a)=-dx^\mu\wedge s(a)$. The linear map $\mathcal E^4_{\epsilon,\alpha}$ writes each ghost-number-one form with its four $dx$ factors on the left, then replaces its single $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ or real $U(1)_V$ ghost jet by the corresponding ordinary parameter jet; it is not an algebra substitution on products of ghosts. The local anomaly class is the class of $I_4^{(1)}$ in $H^{1,4}(s\mid d_H)$: local ghost-number-one four-forms satisfying the second descent equation, modulo $s$-variations of admitted local counterterms and total derivatives.

Then the total perturbative local anomaly class of this conjugate pair vanishes. This conclusion concerns only the identity component of the background-transformation group in the adopted one-loop convention; it asserts no absence of large-transformation or torsion anomalies and no consistency result for a dynamical gauge redundancy.

current_declaration.title: Relative boundary theory and invertible anomaly inflow
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; conditional line-duality and cancellation Definition, with the batch-41 local-anomaly interface inspected and explicitly not used to classify global holonomy. Its Step 1 readiness record is missing; effective dependency level recomputed as 5.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$. Let $Y$ be a compact oriented smooth spin $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $M=\partial Y$, using the outward-normal-first boundary orientation. A background $b$ consists of the metric, spin structure, and any specified principal-bundle connections and associated fields on $Y$; its restriction to $M$ is the boundary background. A $d$-dimensional boundary theory is **relative to an invertible bulk theory** when its partition value is a vector $Z_\partial(M,b|_M)$ in a specified one-dimensional Hermitian line $\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)$, and the bulk assigns the dual line $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\cong\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)^*$ together with a vector $Z_{\mathrm{bulk}}(Y,b)$ in that line. The canonical evaluation

$$\mathrm{ev}:\mathcal L_\partial(M,b|_M)\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}}(M,b|_M)\longrightarrow\mathbb C$$

then defines the combined scalar amplitude. Invertibility means that the bulk assigns a one-dimensional line to each closed $d$-dimensional boundary background and an isomorphism to each bordism map; orientation reversal replaces the assigned line by its dual. For a loop $\gamma$ of compatible background fields and endpoint gauge identifications, the boundary/bulk pair cancels that anomaly along $\gamma$ exactly when

$$\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_\partial)\operatorname{Hol}_{\gamma}(\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk}})=1.$$

The diagram records this condition: the vertical maps are the line evaluation at the two endpoints, and the top map is parallel transport on both lines.

~~~tikzcd
\mathcal L_{\partial,0}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},0}
  \arrow[r,"\mathrm{PT}^{\partial}_{\gamma}\otimes\mathrm{PT}^{\mathrm{bulk}}_{\gamma}"]
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_0"'] &
\mathcal L_{\partial,1}\otimes\mathcal L_{\mathrm{bulk},1}
  \arrow[d,"\mathrm{ev}_1"] \\
\mathbb C \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}_{\mathbb C}"'] & \mathbb C
~~~

current_declaration.title: Symmetry-preserving RG anomaly matching
current_declaration.design_state: A-page conditional equality of the selected anomaly class along the declared exact symmetry-preserving background flow, modulo the stated local counterterms and global holonomies; no phase exclusion or continuum claim.
current_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$. Fix a finite-regulator model on a compact, closed, oriented Riemannian spin four-manifold $M$, with its actual boundary-condition data, fields and jets, regulator, measure, and admissible local counterterms at every scale. Let $G$ be a compact internal global symmetry group with fixed global form, a smooth principal right $G$-bundle $P\to M$, background connection $A$, and unitary finite-dimensional representation $R$. The admitted background groupoid has these nondynamical connections as objects and the selected background gauge transformations as arrows; the symmetry is exact and unbroken along the flow and is not a dynamical gauge redundancy. Fix a smooth family of Fredholm chiral Dirac operators $D^+_{A,R}$ and its inverse determinant line with the Quillen metric and Bismut–Freed unitary connection, as in the determinant-line definition. On each background patch, the finite-regulator partition functional at scale $\mu$ is the local scalar representative of a section of that line, and its transition functions and endpoint gauge actions are retained.

Also fix a Minkowski coordinate region $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with its orientation, spin structure, boundary-term convention, fields and jet domains, and identify it with the Euclidean local-variation problem by a specified Wick-rotation map. Use its background-only finite-jet BRST complex, with nilpotent differential $s$ and horizontal derivative $d_H$; its local anomaly class is the relative cohomology class of ghost-number-one horizontal four-form cocycles modulo $d_H$ and the declared four-dimensional background counterterms. Write $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for the local density whose integral is the counterterm $C$. Assume an exact symmetry-preserving Wilsonian comparison from $\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}$ to $\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}$ retains all remaining low-energy and topological sectors and satisfies $W_{\mu_{\mathrm{UV}}}[A]-W_{\mu_{\mathrm{IR}}}[A]=C[A]$ on each common local branch, for one admissible, single-valued, dimensionless local counterterm. For the determinant-line comparison, take $C$ in the unitary phase convention so $e^{-C[A]}\in U(1)$. Assume the line-valued comparison induces a unitary isomorphism of the endpoint determinant-line families which, in local frames, is multiplication by the phase $e^{-C[A]}$ and which preserves the specified unitary connections and endpoint gauge identifications. Then the ultraviolet and complete infrared four-dimensional local BRST anomaly classes agree modulo the declared local counterterms, and the determinant-line holonomies agree on every admitted loop of background connections modulo gauge transformations. This is a conditional matching constraint only; it determines no infrared spectrum or gap and asserts no continuum limit or empirical result.

current_declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited from the named ADHM and localized equivariant Borel–Moore suppliers; this definition adds no choice principle.
current_declaration.design_state: Step 1 authored; current direct supplier readiness is recorded in the batch notes and decision ledger.
current_declaration.statement:
Fix integers $N\geq2$ and $k\geq0$ and a real stability parameter $\zeta>0$. Let $V=\mathbb C^k$ and $W=\mathbb C^N$ with Hermitian structures. The positive-FI stable complex ADHM quotient $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ is the geometric quotient by $GL(V)$ of quadruples $(B_1,B_2,I,J)$ with $B_i\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$, $I:W\to V$, and $J:V\to W$, satisfying $[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$ and the condition that the vectors $B_{i_1}\cdots B_{i_m}I(w)$ span $V$ for all words of length $m\geq0$ and $w\in W$. This is the positive stability chamber; it is not, by definition, the zero-FI regular quotient or the moduli space of anti-self-dual connections.

Let $T_{\mathbb C}=(\mathbb C^\times)^2\times(\mathbb C^\times)^N$ act algebraically, and let $K=(S^1)^2\times(S^1)^N$ be its maximal compact subgroup. The action is $(t_1,t_2,h)\cdot(B_1,B_2,I,J)=(t_1B_1,t_2B_2,Ih^{-1},t_1t_2hJ)$, where $h$ acts on $W$ with weights $e_\alpha^{-1}$. Thus $\mathbf W=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha^{-1}$ and $\mathbf W^\vee=\sum_{\alpha=1}^N e_\alpha$. Write $\epsilon_i=c_1^K(t_i)$ and $a_\alpha=c_1^K(e_\alpha)$; each has mass dimension one in units $c=\hbar=1$. Let $q$ be a dimensionless formal charge-counting variable.

Assume the complexification of this action gives each $X_{k,N}^\zeta$ a smooth separated finite-type complex structure of dimension $2kN$, a finite invariant affine atlas, and a finite proper fixed locus $F_{k,N}$. Extend the complex torus to $T_m=T_{\mathbb C}\times\mathbb C_m^\times$ with maximal compact subgroup $K_m=K\times S_m^1$; the flavor factor acts trivially on $X_{k,N}^\zeta$. Let $\widetilde m$ be the degree-two equivariant first Chern class of its defining flavor character, let $L_{-1}$ be the associated line of inverse flavor character, and set
$$\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}=c_{2kN}^{T_m}(TX_{k,N}^\zeta\otimes L_{-1})\in H_{T_m}^{4kN}(X_{k,N}^\zeta;\mathbb Q).$$
At a fixed point with tangent weights $w_1,\ldots,w_{2kN}$, its restriction is $\prod_{j=1}^{2kN}(w_j-\widetilde m)$. Let $S_{T_m}$ be generated by the first Chern classes of nontrivial integral characters of $T_m$, put $R_{T_m}=H^*(BK_m;\mathbb Q)=\mathbb Q[\epsilon_1,\epsilon_2,a_1,\ldots,a_N,\widetilde m]$, and let $K_{N,m}=\operatorname{Frac}(R_{T_m})$. When the character-localized Borel–Moore concentration map and proper fixed-locus trace define $p_{k,*}^{\mathrm{loc}}$, set
$$I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)=p_{k,*}^{\mathrm{loc}}\bigl(\mathcal E_{\widetilde m}\cap[X_{k,N}^\zeta]_{K_m}\bigr)\in S_{T_m}^{-1}R_{T_m}\subset K_{N,m}.$$
This is a localized pushforward, not an ordinary pushforward along a nonproper map. The concentration isomorphism and trace are required inputs and are not asserted to exist by this definition.

When these data are supplied for every $k\geq0$, define the coefficientwise formal series
$$Z_{N,\mathrm{adj}}^{\mathrm{loc}}(q;\widetilde m)=\sum_{k\geq0}q^k I_{k,N}^{\mathrm{adj}}(\widetilde m)\in K_{N,m}\langle\!\langle q\rangle\!\rangle.$$
It has no asserted analytic convergence. In the source's Euclidean convention the real mass $m_E$ has mass dimension one, $m=i m_E$, and the equivariant mass is $\widetilde m=m+(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_2)/2$. For the adopted round $S^4_r$ model, $N=2$, $\epsilon_1=\epsilon_2=r^{-1}$, and hence $\widetilde m=i m_E+r^{-1}$. This mass shift is a source-qualified convention. The S4 postulate assumes a supersymmetry-compatible noncommutative regulator agreeing near each pole with the flat-space regulator; it does not construct that regulator or a continuum path-integral measure.

current_declaration.title: Chern character and charge of the normalized twistor monad
current_declaration.statement:
Let $\pi:Z=\mathbb CP^3\to S^4$ be the oriented twistor fibration with the conventions stated in the following references section, let $H=c_1(\mathcal O_Z(1))$, and let $E\to S^4$ be a framed unitary ASD rank-$N$ bundle whose Ward bundle is $\mathcal E=\pi^*E$ as a smooth bundle. Suppose $\mathcal E$ is the cohomology of a linear monad

$$\mathcal O_Z(-1)^{\oplus k}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z^{\oplus(2k+N)}\longrightarrow\mathcal O_Z(1)^{\oplus k}.$$

Then $\operatorname{ch}(\mathcal E)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(\mathcal E)=0$, and $c_2(\mathcal E)=kH^2$. For the twistor orientation specified in the Definition, if $u\in H^4(S^4;\mathbb Z)$ satisfies $\langle u,[S^4]\rangle=1$, then $\pi^*u=H^2$. Consequently

$$k=\langle c_2(E),[S^4]\rangle=-q_N(E,A).$$

current_declaration.title: Restriction of coherent sections to a relatively compact open set is compact
current_declaration.statement: Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb C^m$ be open, and let $\Omega'\subseteq\Omega$ be open with compact closure contained in $\Omega$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic module on a neighborhood of $\overline\Omega'$. Suppose it has a finite presentation by free sheaves on $\Omega$ and that the presentation section maps on both $\Omega$ and $\Omega'$ are surjective. Give the two section spaces the quotient topologies from compact-convergence on the finite free section spaces. current_declaration.title: Constant flat summands of positive real monads
current_declaration.axiom_base: ZF + full AC inherited through the analytic scalar-cohomology input; the finite orthogonal splitting is choice-free.
current_declaration.statement:
Let
$$
\mathcal O(-1)\otimes U\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal O\otimes S\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal O(1)\otimes U'
$$
be a locally split linear monad on $\mathbb P^3(\mathbb C)$ with locally free middle cohomology $F$. Suppose a nondegenerate Hermitian form $H$ on $S$, linear in the first variable, satisfies $\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ for $j(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2)=(-\bar\lambda_2,\bar\lambda_1,-\bar\mu_2,\bar\mu_1)$. Assume $H^0(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$, $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ for every $q\ge0$, and $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. Define $L=\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i\subseteq S$ and $M=\sum_i\operatorname{im}\alpha_i\subseteq S$, where $\alpha(z)=\sum_i z_i\alpha_i$ and $\beta(z)=\sum_i z_i\beta_i$. If the Hermitian form induced by $H$ on $H^0(F|_\ell)$ is positive definite for every $\sigma$-invariant real line $\ell$, then $H^0(F)=L=M^{\perp_H}$, $H|_L$ is positive definite, and $S=L\oplus M$ is an $H$-orthogonal decomposition. The monad and its pairing split as the constant summand $L\otimes\mathcal O$ plus the reduced monad $U\otimes\mathcal O(-1)\to M\otimes\mathcal O\to U'\otimes\mathcal O(1)$; the reduced cohomology has no global sections and remains positive on every real line. The conclusion includes $U=0$, when $L=S$ and $M=0$.

current_declaration.title: N=1 Wilsonian F-Term Nonrenormalization
current_declaration.statement: Let a local rigid four-dimensional N=1 superspace action datum have the form fixed above, including its canonical matter kinetic term, with finite-dimensional unitary matter representations of a fixed compact gauge group, an additional real D-term integrand $G$, a holomorphic gauge-invariant F-term integrand $F(\Phi,W)$, and a formal Wilsonian cutoff prescription at a nonzero scale $0<\lambda<\Lambda_0$. Assume the selected prescription has the local nondynamical-spurion extension specified in the action data and supplies the one-particle-irreducible cutoff vertex functional and a local derivative expansion coefficientwise in formal perturbation theory around the topologically trivial background, as specified above. Let $\langle\cdot\rangle_\lambda$ be the normalized coefficientwise expectation of the selected regulated formal expansion. Assume its rigid N=1 and BRST changes of variables obey $\langle\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}\mathcal O\rangle_\lambda=\langle\mathcal O\,\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}S_\lambda\rangle_\lambda$ and $\langle s\mathcal O\rangle_\lambda=0$ for every local insertion $\mathcal O$, with counterterms satisfying the same identities and no local gauge anomaly. Then the Wilsonian chiral integrand is unchanged coefficientwise, $F_\lambda(\Phi,W)=F(\Phi,W)$; the holomorphic gauge-coupling parameters may receive one-loop corrections, but no higher-loop corrections. If an unbroken U(1) factor is present, a Fayet–Iliopoulos parameter can receive a correction only at one loop, and that correction is proportional to the sum of the U(1) charges of all left-chiral multiplets, including multiplicities; it vanishes when this charge sum is zero. The theorem imposes no nonrenormalization condition on the additional real D-term integrand $G_\lambda$, the Kähler data, or coefficients expressed after a scale-dependent chiral-field rescaling that normalizes a positive real quadratic kinetic form. It is only a formal perturbative Wilsonian statement at nonzero cutoff: it does not assert nonperturbative exactness, a result for an arbitrary one-particle-irreducible functional, or existence of a continuum interacting quantum field theory.

current_declaration.statement:
Use the flat four-dimensional background data with global group $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ and the common consistent regulator fixed above. Take the finite spectrum to consist of positive-chirality Weyl species $E=(\mathbf3,+1)$ and $E^*=(\bar{\mathbf3},-1)$. On a formal six-dimensional extension, write the anti-Hermitian $SU(3)$ curvature as $F_A$ and the $U(1)_V$ curvature as $f=dB$. $$\mathcal I_6(E)=\frac{i}{24\pi^2}\left(\operatorname{tr}F_A^3+3i f\wedge\operatorname{tr}F_A^2+3(if)^3\right).$$

current_declaration.title: A fixed source breaks the matching symmetry
current_declaration.design_state: B-page finite four-dimensional scalar-lattice endpoint with a fixed source; checks explicit breaking and the failure of the theorem hypothesis.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $\Lambda_a=(a\mathbb Z/Na\mathbb Z)^4$ be the periodic four-dimensional lattice with $N\geq2$ sites in each direction and spacing $a>0$; each coordinate is taken modulo $Na$. At each site $x$ take a complex scalar $\phi_x$ of mass dimension one. In natural units $c=\hbar=1$, choose a mass $m_0>0$ and a dimensionless coupling $\lambda>0$, and define the finite Euclidean action

$$
S_j[\phi]=a^4\sum_{x\in\Lambda_a}\left(\sum_{\nu=1}^{4}\left|\frac{\phi_{x+a\hat\nu}-\phi_x}{a}\right|^2+m_0^2|\phi_x|^2+\lambda|\phi_x|^4+j(\phi_x+\overline{\phi_x})\right),
$$

where the fixed real source $j\neq0$ has mass dimension three. The finite-dimensional Lebesgue integral converges because the positive quartic term dominates the linear source. The source-free action has a global $U(1)$ transformation $\phi_x\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\phi_x$, but the fixed-source theory does not. Consequently this endpoint fails the exact-symmetry hypothesis of the anomaly-matching theorem; the example asserts no change, absence, or value of an anomaly.

current_declaration.title: A mixed-background counterterm shift along RG
current_declaration.design_state: B-page worked small-gauge U(1)^3 background counterterm variation on a closed four-torus; verifies equality of the four-dimensional local anomaly classes.
current_declaration.statement:
Let $M=T^4$ be a closed flat Euclidean four-torus. Fix three nondynamical $U(1)$ background connections $A_1,A_2,A_3$, each a globally defined real 1-form on the trivial bundle, and allow only gauge transformations $A_i\mapsto A_i+d\lambda_i$ with smooth single-valued periodic real functions $\lambda_i$. Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$, so $[A_i]=$ mass, $[F_i]=$ mass squared, and the functional below is dimensionless. In a declared counterterm scheme, take the allowed local background counterterm

$$
C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4} A_1\wedge A_2\wedge F_3,
$$

where $F_3=dA_3$ and $k\in\mathbb R$ is a fixed dimensionless coefficient. Suppose an exact background-coupled RG comparison has $W_{\mathrm{UV}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]=W_{\mathrm{IR}}[A_1,A_2,A_3]+C_k[A_1,A_2,A_3]$ on this background domain. Then the two local anomaly representatives differ by

$$
\delta C_k=\frac{ik}{2\pi}\int_{T^4}\bigl(-\lambda_1 F_2\wedge F_3+\lambda_2 F_1\wedge F_3\bigr),\qquad F_i=dA_i,
$$

and therefore define the same local anomaly class modulo the declared counterterms.

current_declaration.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ on the four-dimensional affine Minkowski space $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, as in the selected HEFT spacetime convention. Use the trivial spin structure, spinor bundle $S=M\times\mathbb C^4$, gamma matrices satisfying $\{\gamma^\mu,\gamma^\nu\}=2\eta^{\mu\nu}I$, chirality operator $\gamma_5=i\gamma^0\gamma^1\gamma^2\gamma^3$, and eigensubbundles $S_\pm=\ker(\gamma_5\mp I)$. Take the trivial bundle for the fixed global symmetry group $H=SU(3)\times U(1)_V$, set the $SU(3)$ background connection to zero, and keep only the nondynamical $U(1)_V$ connection $B\in\Omega_c^1(M,\mathbb R)$ with curvature $G=dB$. Here $U(1)_V=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}$ and its charge-$q$ representation is $\rho_q(z)=z^q$ on $\mathbb C$. The background $B$ is not integrated over as a quantum gauge redundancy.

Let $\psi_+\in C_c^\infty(M,S_+\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,+1)})$ and $\psi_-\in C_c^\infty(M,S_-\otimes\mathbb C_{(\mathbf1,0)})$ be complex Weyl fields in the indicated $SU(3)\times U(1)_V$ representations. Use $D_q=d+iqB$ on charge-$q$ fields and the fixed Lorentz-scalar chiral Dirac pairing $\bar\psi_+\psi_-$. Let $\Phi=v e^{i\theta}$ be a nonvanishing order-parameter field in $(\mathbf1,+1)$ with fixed modulus $v>0$ and smooth real phase $\theta\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. A dimensionless nonzero Yukawa parameter $y$ gives the mass term $-y\Phi\bar\psi_+\psi_-+\mathrm{h.c.}$, where h.c. denotes Hermitian conjugation, and heavy mass $M_H=|y|v>0$. The fermion fields have mass dimension $3/2$, $v$ and $M_H$ have mass dimension one, $B_\mu$ has mass dimension one, $G_{\mu\nu}$ has mass dimension two, and $\theta$ is dimensionless.

For $\alpha\in C_c^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, use $B\mapsto B+d\alpha$, $\psi_+\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\psi_+$, $\psi_-\mapsto\psi_-$, and $\Phi\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\Phi$, hence $\theta\mapsto\theta-\alpha$. These transformations leave the Yukawa term invariant. In the anti-Hermitian product-group convention, the selected singlet has connection $iB$ and covariant derivative $d+iB$; in Bilal's Hermitian convention write $\mathscr A=-B$ and $\epsilon=-\alpha$, so $d-i\mathscr A=d+iB$ and the transformations agree. Let $\Gamma_H[B,\theta]$ denote the formal one-loop effective-action contribution of this fermion pair with the Pauli–Villars subtraction used for the chiral triangle: include a physical loop with $M_0=0$ and three regulator loops with statistics weights $\eta_0=\eta_2=1$ and $\eta_1=\eta_3=-1$, choose a positive scale $M_{\mathrm{PV}}$ and masses $M_1=M_3=M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, $M_2=\sqrt2M_{\mathrm{PV}}$, and take $M_{\mathrm{PV}}\to\infty$ after the subtraction. Define the consistent anomaly as the infinitesimal variation of this effective action, rather than as a covariant-current divergence. Add no non-invariant local counterterm to $\Gamma_H$; gauge-invariant local counterterms may be added. For an undetermined real coefficient $c$, the candidate Wess–Zumino functional is $\Gamma_c[B,\theta]=c\int_M\theta G\wedge G$; the theorem on this page fixes $c$.

As a source-backed threshold input, adopt the following scope-limited consequence of the heavy-fermion field-redefinition argument: removing the phase of a Yukawa-generated heavy chiral mass by a chiral redefinition transfers that phase to the regulated measure, whose consistent anomalous variation is independent of the heavy mass. This supplies the local Wess–Zumino threshold interpretation when $\theta$ is retained; it is not a construction of the full determinant or a bound on all remaining terms. Let $E$ be a positive mass scale bounding absolute external momentum components in these coordinates. The threshold regime is $E/M_H\ll1$, with no Lorentz-invariant norm or expansion-remainder bound asserted. All determinant and anomaly data here are formal perturbative inputs; no exact functional integral or continuum limit is claimed.
